fragments.text: Target edition: 17 October 2026. Blotter is the practice manager a US bookkeeping or accounting firm uses to complete client engagements from signed scope through recurring work, communications, document collection, review and payment. It replaces Karbon, TaxDome or Canopy and offers the connected close and small-firm automation depth buyers seek from Financial Cents and Double. USD and US practice norms are the default. Difficulty building provider applications, bank/payment connections, desktop bridges or native apps is work to deliver, not a smaller product boundary.

This is the product destination. Status below describes current code, not a reduction of that destination. The previous first-release ACCEPTANCE.md described an Australian BAS-style workflow with manual deadlines, link uploads, independent review and billing CSVs; there was no root CONTRACT.md or existing product clause ID to rename. Its useful guarantees are retained here. The Status table classifies each clause as published, target or push-further, including implemented foundations. Existing UI, homepage and runtime behavior are unchanged by this document.
| Category | Accounting practice management software |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Karbon, TaxDome, Canopy, Financial Cents, Double |
| First buyer | A US principal or operations manager of a bookkeeping or accounting firm with 1–15 staff, running recurring client engagements and tax-season work |

Every named clause gives buyer behavior and an acceptance journey through the app, authenticated HTTP API, CLI or authorized provider door. ACCEPTANCE.md lists the same journeys and statuses. A cited local file/test proves only its stated implemented subset; it does not prove real-provider acceptance, tax authority access, native distribution, production capacity or accessibility. Real-provider journeys use authorized accounts; automated tests fake only paid/network edges. Source freshness, provider acknowledgment, settlement and human judgment are distinct facts.

Current statuses describe this candidate tree. The exact commit and its verification runs are reported in the branch handoff; a status claim is counted only after the guarded landing and CT judgment. Due dates are recorded by people, set by WORK-002 rules or calculated from approved deadline rules (DUE-001, DUE-003).

**US-001 — US firm setup and currency.** A US principal configures a firm in USD with US addresses, EIN/entity classifications, fiscal years, service lines, time zones and notification hours. Money uses integer cents and explicit currency; US 1099/W-2, federal/state tax and sales-tax engagements have appropriate terminology. Historical AUD records retain their currency and are never relabeled USD. **Acceptance evidence:** Set up a US bookkeeping and tax practice, add an LLC and individual client, select USD and America/New_York, and create payroll, sales-tax and annual-tax work. Inspect currency and dates across a daylight-saving change; imported AUD history remains AUD. **Implemented currency and identifiers (US-001):** New templates, rates and native prospects default to USD; each stored fee, time entry and expense carries its currency. Existing money rows and historical export snapshots remain AUD, with no conversion or relabeling. Jobs inherit their template currency, time requires a rate in that currency, mixed-currency exports are refused, and WIP, reimbursement and pipeline fee totals are grouped by currency. New client EINs accept nine digits; eleven-digit ABNs remain legacy ABNs. Native and CSV inputs retain that distinction, and search keeps SEARCH-001 role restrictions and last-four masking. The demo uses US filings and America/New_York office instants, using each date’s daylight-saving offset. **Firm settings (US-001):** the principal records the firm name, US street/city/state/ZIP address, nine-digit EIN, entity classification, fiscal year-end month/day, service lines, default USD or AUD currency, IANA time zone and staff email notification hours. New templates, hourly rates and native prospects use the firm default unless explicitly overridden; historical money and exports never change. Workspace activity instants and today use the firm zone with its date-specific daylight-saving offset; date-only deadlines keep their recorded day. A recorded filing calendar holds a name, jurisdiction, date and required source or firm-defined label: these are human-entered dates, not automatic agency calculations (DUE-001/003). Notification start is inclusive and end exclusive in the firm zone; an earlier end spans midnight and equal times allow all day. In-app alerts appear immediately; staff emails outside the window remain durably deferred until the hourly trigger runs inside it. Completed attempts are not resent, and inactive recipients are not mailed. Client sends and sign-in mail keep their current behavior. Settings and calendars survive practice archive restore. Future notification channels (NOTIFY-001), connected-mail schedules (MAIL-003), automation (AUTOMATE-001), and deadline calculations (DUE-001/003) inherit the firm zone and applicable notification hours before shipping; CRM-001 carries client entity/contact structure and phone/SSN-digit matching for CRM-004 and SEARCH-001. **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** The firm's US postal address appears on every marketing email, and a marketing send without it is refused.

**CRM-001 — Client entities and contacts.** Manage individuals, businesses and trusts with multiple contacts, authorized signers, portal users, responsible partner, assigned team, service scope, lifecycle and consent preferences. Contacts carry roles (primary, billing, tax, bookkeeping) that route invoices, requests and signatures. A contact may represent several entities without sharing their private records; duplicates are merged under CRM-004. Search, edit, archive and reactivate clients without losing engagement history. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a business with two contacts and an individual linked to its owner; assign different staff and portal permissions, change a contact, archive/reactivate the business and inspect retained jobs. A contact without entity authority cannot read its records. **Inherited CRM-005:** CRM-005 prospect contacts, including every additional authorized contact, move to the one converted client before this ships. **Implemented semantics (ct 19 Oct 12:58Z):** an entity is an individual, business or trust; its responsible partner is an active reviewer or principal, its assigned team lists active staff, and services and a related owner/household client are recorded without granting job access. Each contact relationship belongs to one entity; the same normalized email may represent several entities without pooling authority. Staff explicitly record primary/billing/tax/bookkeeping roles, signer authority, portal permission and request/email consent, with a note. Existing single contacts retain only their existing entity's collection authority. Requests and deliverables choose an authorized, consented recipient explicitly or the unique primary contact; ambiguous primaries refuse a send. A job link authenticates possession only and is bound to that entity/contact; contact edits revoke its old links, and every portal read/write rechecks active entity, authority and consent. PORTAL-002 inherits identified portal accounts, recovery and MFA; BILL-002 and SIGN-001/SIGN-002/ENGAGE-001 inherit billing/tax/signer routing before those capabilities ship. ACCESS-002 inherits configurable staff grants; assignments today never widen existing job visibility. Archive blocks new work, recurrence generation and client sends while preserving engagements/history; reactivation allows fresh links but never revives revoked ones. Phone normalization removes punctuation, adds +1 to ten-digit US numbers and otherwise requires a country code (8–15 digits); duplicate proposals use exact normalized phone. Individuals store only four SSN digits, never a full SSN; matching/search is principal/reviewer-only and output is masked. Contact merges need the principal's per-contact recorded authority whenever either side would gain records, preserve distinct relationships without combining consent, revoke old links, and support CRM-004's unchanged 30-day undo. Prospect conversion copies all additional contacts once. Offboarding previews and transfers partner/team responsibilities; archive restore preserves contact grants and lifecycle. **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** Marketing grants are recorded per contact relationship, withdrawals apply to the address across the whole firm, and a marketing grant never restores email consent.

**CRM-002 — Client groups and custom fields.** Group related entities and households, capture typed firm-defined fields and tags, filter a segment and apply reviewed bulk updates or work creation. Required-field validation and permissions apply to imported and API-created records too. **Acceptance evidence:** Group a parent, subsidiary and household; add a fiscal-year and service-tier field, filter the group and schedule its annual work. Preview a bulk field change, reject one invalid value and confirm unrelated clients are unchanged.

**CRM-003 — Engagement history and accountable ownership.** Each client and engagement has a searchable chronological history of email, portal messages, documents, requests, assignments, reviews, deadlines, signed scope and billing outcomes. Every unresolved item has a responsible person, next action and due condition; closing a message alone does not complete the engagement. **Acceptance evidence:** Open a client after two periods of work and trace a request from email through upload, review and payment. Filter unresolved items, change their owner and inspect authors, source links and timestamps; a preparer sees only authorized history. **Semantics (CRM-003):** a client's history is every audited action on the client, its jobs and their requests, files, discussions, notices, expenses, time and recurring rules, and the billing exports that include its work, newest first, each with its author, UTC time and the job it links to, searchable by text and filtered by kind (documents, assignments, reviews, deadlines, messages, billing). Unresolved items are open requests (owner: the job's preparer), open tasks (their named or role owner), jobs in review (the reviewer), open discussions (their owner) and open notices (their assignee), each with its next action and due condition (the job's due date, a follow-up date or a response date), filterable by owner; resolving a discussion completes nothing else. A reviewer or the principal hands an item to another person: a request's owner is its job's preparer and a review's its reviewer, so those reassign the job and nobody is made to review their own work; a task is assigned by name (WORK-009 read access); a discussion goes only to someone who can read it; every handover is audited. A preparer sees only the jobs they may read (ACCESS-001), and client-wide records and exports only reach reviewers and the principal. Today's email is the document reminder; connected-mailbox email (MAIL-001), portal messages (PORTAL-003), signed scope (ENGAGE-001), invoices (BILL-002) and payments (PAY-001) write their events into this history, with author, time and source link and the same visibility, before they ship. **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** Bulk messages and their delivery, bounce, complaint and reply events file to each client's history under their class, engagement or marketing.

**CRM-004 — Merge duplicate clients and contacts.** Blotter proposes likely duplicate clients and contacts after an import, email auto-match, portal sign-up or connector sync, using matching email, phone, EIN, last four SSN digits and name similarity. Staff compare the records side by side, choose the surviving value for each field and merge. Work, tasks, email threads, documents, organizers, signatures, invoices, payments, portal users and history move to the survivor with an audit record. Source IDs from both records (Karbon, TaxDome, Canopy, QBO, Xero) stay attached so later imports and syncs match the survivor. A merge that would give one contact access to another entity's private records without authority is refused. An unchanged merge can be undone for 30 days. **Acceptance evidence:** Import a Karbon client that duplicates a native client and accept the suggested match. Choose field values, merge, and inspect the moved jobs, email, invoices and portal access on the survivor with exactly one QBO mapping. Undo the merge before further edits and inspect the restored records; then repeat the merge, re-run the import and confirm it matches the survivor without creating a duplicate. A merge joining two unrelated entities' contacts without authority is refused. **Matching (implemented subset):** proposals are worked out from the clients as they are when read, whatever created them; a pair is proposed when it shares a contact email (case-insensitive), a non-empty EIN (the client's tax id), or a name that is equal, or similar (at least two words each and at least 75% of their distinct words shared), once lower-cased and with accents, punctuation, "&"/"and" and business suffixes set aside. Phone and last-four SSN matches join when CRM-001 stores them, before CRM-001 ships (ct 19 Oct 11:47Z). A person may record, with a reason, that a proposed pair is two different clients; it is not proposed again. **Authority (ct 19 Oct 03:36Z):** a merge of two clients with different non-empty EINs, or different non-empty contact emails, needs the principal's recorded authority reason (same entity; the surviving contact is authorized for both); reviewers merge only records whose EINs and contact emails agree or are blank; CRM-001 contacts and PORTAL-002 portal users add a per-contact check before they ship. Undo is available for 30 days while neither record has changed since the merge. **Merge and undo (semantics):** the person picks which client keeps its id (the survivor) and, for every field where the two differ (name, EIN, contact name and email, tags and each firm field), which value survives; each client keeps its own "came from" source. The other client stays as a read-only record pointing at the survivor and leaves every list and picker. Its jobs (with their tasks, time, documents, organizer answers, deliverables and upload links), discussions, tax notices, expenses, recurring rules, rate cards and group memberships move to the survivor, including signed-off jobs, resolved discussions, closed notices and decided or reimbursed expenses, whose only permitted change is that move, between the two clients of a merge that is not undone. A merge is refused while both clients have a job from the same template for the same period, or a recurring rule for the same template. Moved rate cards join the survivor's under TIME-003 precedence. Each import source row keeps the client it created; a re-import of that row still matches it, shows the survivor it now lives on and creates no client. Undo restores the recorded records, memberships and the survivor's own values exactly; it is open until the merge time plus 30 × 24 hours while the survivor has not been edited, merged again, or gained or lost a linked record since, and changes made inside moved records travel back with them. A merge made on the principal's authority is undone only by the principal. **Inherited:** each later capability moves with a merge and keeps its source IDs attached before it ships: CRM-001 contacts (including phone and SSN-digit matches), MAIL-001 email threads, BILL-002 invoices, PAY-001 payments, PORTAL-002 portal users, PORTAL-004 organizers, SIGN-001/SIGN-002 signatures, and the source IDs of MIGRATE-001–005 (Karbon, TaxDome, Canopy, Financial Cents, Double) and LEDGER-001/INTEGRATE-001 (QBO, Xero; exactly one ledger mapping per survivor). **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** Merging two contacts keeps the most restrictive marketing consent, and undo restores each side exactly. Implemented and asserted on MSG-002's doors (consent carriers journey, `tests/blotter/bulk-messages.test.mjs`); MSG-002 states the exact semantics.

**CRM-005 — Prospects intake and onboarding pipeline.** Track prospects through firm-defined stages (for example inquiry, consult booked, proposal sent, won, lost) with lead source, requested services, estimated annual fees and owner. An embeddable, spam-protected website intake form creates a prospect with its answers and uploads. A consult can be booked under INTEGRATE-005 and a proposal sent under ENGAGE-001 or INTEGRATE-004. Winning converts the prospect into exactly one client with contacts, signed scope and documents and starts onboarding work. Lost prospects keep a required reason. A pipeline report shows conversion, stage age and fee totals by source and owner. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit the embedded intake form and inspect the new prospect with source and answers; a spam submission is rejected. Book a consult, send a proposal and accept it; confirm one client with contacts, signed scope and onboarding work, and repeat the acceptance event without a second client. Mark another prospect lost with a reason and inspect the pipeline report's conversion, stage age and fee totals. **Semantics (CRM-005):** the principal and reviewers record and move prospects (as they add clients); Inquiry, Consult booked, Proposal sent, Won and Lost are built in and the principal adds open stages between them by position. A prospect carries its name, contact, lead source, requested services, estimated annual fees (integer cents) and owner (an active member); every stage change is kept with who and when. Moving to Lost needs a reason; Won is reached only by winning. Winning converts the prospect, in one batch, into exactly one client (its name and contact, the firm's required client fields supplied) and starts its onboarding job from a chosen template (preparer, reviewer, period, due date and its source); a repeated win returns that client and job and creates nothing, and a won prospect cannot be moved or lost again. The pipeline report, as of now in whole UTC days rounded down, gives per lead source and per owner the prospects, open, won and lost counts, conversion (won as a whole percentage of won plus lost; none until one closes) and open, won and lost fee totals grouped by stored currency, and per open stage the prospects in it with their average and oldest days in that stage. **Public intake (CRM-005; ct 19 Oct 10:05Z):** `/intake` alone permits embedding (`frame-ancestors *`). A required consent line records that details go only to the practice to reply to this inquiry. Accepted forms create an Inquiry owned by the principal with lead source, requested services, free-text answers and an optional annual-budget band (not a quote), consent wording/time and up to three attachments of at most 1 MiB each. Spam checks are a honeypot, an installation-signed single-use form token valid from 3 seconds through 24 hours after issue, and at most five accepted submissions per connection in a rolling hour. Rejected submissions store no prospect, answers or uploads. Rate-limit IPs are kept only as installation-keyed digests with one-hour expiry, excluded from archives and cleared on accepted submissions and the hourly trigger; raw IPs are never stored. Turnstile runs only when the owner supplies both keys. Only the principal and reviewers read intake answers/uploads. Winning files the intake uploads on the client's onboarding work in the same batch without retaining a second copy of their bytes; the original intake links still resolve. Owner-confirmed attachment erasure follows ERASURE-001 and fences stale archives; intake prospects, answers, consent records and uploads inherit CRM target erasure and retention under ERASURE-002 before it ships. **Inherited before shipping (ct 19 Oct 10:28Z):** consult booking (INTEGRATE-005), proposal sending, accepted signed scope and signed documents (ENGAGE-001/INTEGRATE-004), and additional contacts (CRM-001) each connect to this idempotent win before shipping; no manual win claims a proposal was sent or signed. CRM-005 is done for the native pipeline and intake that exist today. **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** The public intake form may offer only an optional, unticked marketing checkbox with its exact wording, separate from the reply consent; its grant follows the prospect's contact to the converted client. Implemented and asserted on MSG-002's doors (consent carriers journey, `tests/blotter/bulk-messages.test.mjs`); MSG-002 states the exact semantics.

**ENGAGE-001 — Proposals engagement letters and signatures.** Build service proposals and versioned engagement letters with scope, exclusions, USD fees, retainer terms, renewal and amendment rules. Send to authorized signers, collect electronic signatures with signer authority, consent, timestamps and a downloadable certificate, then launch onboarding once. Preserve declined, expired, superseded and partially signed states. IRS e-file signature authorizations (Forms 8879, 8879-S, 8879-PE, 8879-C, 8879-F and 8878) are owned by SIGN-001, which states the signers, KBA, fallback, record and retention rules; other signed documents use SIGN-002. **Acceptance evidence:** Send a two-signer proposal, amend it before completion and verify the old version cannot bind the new terms. Complete signatures, download the signed letter/certificate and inspect one onboarding job; decline another and inspect its retained declined state. Collect a married-filing-jointly Form 8879 under SIGN-001's acceptance. **Engagement history (CRM-003, inherited before this ships):** sent, amended, signed and declined scope appear in the client's history with author, time and source link, visible only to those who may read the job, and any unresolved item they create (an unsigned proposal) names an owner, next action and due condition. **Acceptance evidence (CRM-003):** the signed letter appears in the client history with its signer and time. **Inherited CRM-005:** CRM-005 proposal sending and acceptance attach the accepted signed scope/documents to its client and invoke its idempotent win exactly once before this ships. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** Marketing consent is never bundled into an engagement letter or signature, nor made a condition of service. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, its signed letters and certificates join ERASURE-002's signed-engagement class with that clause's clock, holds, preview, receipt and fence, and its signing provider's copies are named outside copies; practitioner-recorded engagements keep their label (ct 22 Oct 2026).

**SIGN-001 — IRS e-file signature authorizations with KBA.** Blotter collects IRS e-file signature authorizations: Forms 8879, 8879-S, 8879-PE, 8879-C, 8879-F and 8878. The practitioner attaches the final form produced by the tax software (INTEGRATE-002) to the client-year return engagement. Blotter sends it to every required signer: both spouses for married filing jointly, an officer for an 1120-S or 1120, and a partner or LLC member for a 1065. For remote signing, each signer passes knowledge-based authentication (KBA) through the identity provider, with their own credentials. A failed KBA attempt can be retried. After three failed attempts, electronic signing stops for that signer and Blotter creates a handwritten-signature task with the printable form, following the IRS e-signature rules for these forms. The record kept against the return engagement contains the signed PDF, the provider certificate and audit trail, and for each signer the name, timestamp, IP address, login ID and every KBA result. It also holds the document hash. The record is kept for at least three years from the return due date or the IRS received date, whichever is later, and ERASURE-002 cannot delete it sooner. Until every required signature is present, the work item cannot enter its ready-to-file status (WORK-007). Blotter never marks a return filed: transmitted, accepted and rejected states come only from INTEGRATE-008 evidence. FOLLOWUP-001 chases unsigned forms. **Acceptance evidence:** Attach a Form 8879 to a married-filing-jointly 1040 engagement and send it to both spouses through the KBA provider at its test edge. Make one spouse fail KBA once and pass on retry. Make the second spouse fail three times, and confirm electronic signing is refused for them and a handwritten-signature task with the printable form is created. Before both signatures exist, moving the work to ready to file is refused. After the wet signature is uploaded, the move is allowed. Inspect the stored signed PDF, certificate, per-signer IP address, login ID and KBA attempts on the 1040 engagement, and confirm a retention date three years after the later of due date and received date. Erasure before that date is refused. The return stays unfiled until an INTEGRATE-008 acceptance arrives, and an unsigned form is chased under FOLLOWUP-001. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Its record is ERASURE-002's IRS e-file authorization class.

**SIGN-002 — General document signature requests.** Staff request signatures on any firm document, for example a Form 2848 or 8821 (AUTHZ-001), a bank authorization, a management representation letter or a W-9. They place signature, initial, date and text fields on the PDF and choose one or more signers in sequential or parallel order. Signers give ESIGN Act and UETA consent, or pass KBA when the form requires it. Requests can be voided, declined with a reason and resent. FOLLOWUP-001 chases unsigned requests. The signed PDF and its certificate are filed to the client and work item with a timeline entry. **Acceptance evidence:** Place fields on a PDF and request sequential signatures from two contacts. The first signer declines with a reason; resend the request, then complete both signatures. Inspect the signed file, its certificate, the signing order and the timeline on the client and work item. A voided request cannot be signed afterwards, and a contact who is not a signer cannot open it. **Offboarding (ACCESS-006, inherited before this ships):** pending signature requests sent in a departing staff member's name appear in the offboarding preview and move to the work successor in its approved batch; completed signatures keep their original requester. **Acceptance evidence (ACCESS-006):** offboard a preparer with a pending signature request; it is listed, follows the successor, and no request is left owned by the deactivated member. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** Marketing consent is never bundled into a signature request, nor made a condition of service. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, SIGN-002 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026). **Native semantics (sx-blotter-c36/c37, 22 Oct; approved with change by ct, batch 11 H):** Staff with full job scope freeze the original valid unencrypted PDF, signer relationships, order and signature/initial/date/text field geometry, then explicitly send through existing entity/contact-bound portal links. Every contact signer must be active, authorized for the entity, a signer, portal-enabled and consented for requests/email; a staff representative signer is an active member or the principal who holds the client with working access. The portal exposes only that signer's fields and requires explicit document-specific ESIGN/UETA consent and intent, never marketing consent. Sequential signatures wait for every prior signer; parallel signatures can arrive in either order, with revision guards preventing lost updates. Decline records a reason; resending a declined or restored request starts a fresh attempt and preserves prior attempts. Voiding prevents further signatures. Completion flattens entered fields onto the original PDF and creates a separate downloadable certificate with order, name, contact/link id, consent wording/version, times and document hashes. It truthfully states typed electronic signatures and portal-possession authentication, not verified identity, KBA or a cryptographic digital signature. **Ruled (ct 22 Oct):** at consent and at signing, Blotter records the connection IP and user agent. Both appear on the certificate and are retained and erased with the signed record. For a document marked Form 2848 or 8821, a signer's signature is accepted only after a staff member records a remote-authentication attestation: the method (photo ID by selfie or video plus a secondary document, or personal knowledge), the verifier, the date and the items checked. The certificate states the form is electronically signed and may be submitted only online at IRS.gov/Submit2848. Staff representatives can be signers through their own session. A PDF whose text names Form 8879, 8879-S/PE/C/F or 8878 is refused for SIGN-001. **Semantic implemented (sx-blotter-c37):** consent and signature are one explicit submission, so the connection IP (the edge's connecting address) and user agent are captured once at that moment for each signer, stored only on the signer record, printed on the certificate as the consent-and-signature connection, and redacted with the signer record when the signed record is erased; they never enter the audit log. A document is a Form 2848 or 8821 when its form kind, title or the PDF's own text names it; the attestation is recorded per remote (contact) signer and signing attempt by a staff member with the job, with method photo ID by selfie or video (name, SSN or ITIN, address and date of birth checked against a named secondary document) or personal knowledge (with how it was established), the verifier's name and a date not in the future; it cannot be changed once recorded, and a resend needs a fresh attestation. A staff representative is named as a signer, receives no portal link, and signs with the same consent and intent at `/signatures/:id/staff-sign` in their own authenticated session (the session id stands in for the portal link on the certificate); they need no attestation. The 8879/8878 check reads the PDF text as well as the form kind, title and file name. A deactivated staff signer can no longer sign; the request is voided and re-requested. AUTHZ-001 inherits this attestation and the Submit2848 statement when it prepares 2848/8821 records. Staff/client work views file the signed PDF, certificate and timeline on the source client/work. Pending requests move atomically during offboarding; completed requester attribution stays. Signature-complete events use existing notification preferences, quiet hours, live authority and deduplication, and the automation source is rechecked inside its once-only effect batch. Signed documents join ERASURE-002 signed_documents clocks from completion or later job sign-off, class/job/record holds, preview, expiry, counts, receipt and stale-restore fence; unfinished requests block erasure until completed or voided. Restored pending/declined requests stay held and old bearer links remain excluded. Outside mail/download copies name their holders. Erased-client signed records disappear from normal lists and use opaque expiry labels; explicit retained detail/PDF doors require the principal and attribute the read. SIGN-001 retains its separate required KBA and IP/login/KBA-result evidence; general signing refuses IRS e-file authorization forms (by label or PDF text) or any form marked KBA-required until that provider path ships. FOLLOWUP-001 inherits unsigned-request chasing before its schedule door ships.

**AUTHZ-001 — Taxpayer authorizations 2848 and 8821.** Track IRS Form 2848 powers of attorney, Form 8821 tax information authorizations and state equivalents for each client. Each record holds the representative and CAF number, the tax matters, forms and periods covered, the signature date, the submission method (IRS online submission, Tax Pro Account or fax) and the recorded, rejected or withdrawn status. Blotter prepares the form from client and representative data for signature under SIGN-002 and files the signed copy. Transcript requests (INTEGRATE-006) and agency contact on notices (DUE-002) are blocked outside the scope of a recorded authorization. An alert fires before the covered periods run out for continuing engagements. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a 2848 covering Form 1040 for 2022–2025, collect the client's and representative's signatures, and record its online submission and CAF-recorded status. Request a 2021 transcript and confirm it is blocked as outside the authorization's scope, while a 2024 request proceeds. Withdraw the authorization and confirm the dependent notice work is flagged and new transcript requests are refused. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping. **Implemented native policy (sx-blotter-c37/c38, 22 Oct):** the principal or a reviewer records a client's Form 2848, Form 8821 or state authorization (representative, optional staff representative and CAF number, and one to ten tax matters with form and first/last year) as a draft; files its signed copy by linking a completed SIGN-002 request (a 2848 or 8821 only through a request that carried the remote-authentication attestation); records the submission (an electronically signed 2848 or 8821 only as IRS online submission, per IRS.gov/Submit2848); and records the agency's answer (recorded with the CAF number, or rejected with its reason) or a withdrawal. A transcript request is recorded only inside a recorded 2848 or 8821 covering its form and year (retrieval is INTEGRATE-006). Agency contact on a DUE-002 notice needs a recorded 2848 (federal) or the state agency's recorded authorization covering the year in the notice's tax period. Withdrawal writes a flag into the timeline of each open notice it covered, ends its transcript requests and refuses new ones. From October 1 of an authorization's last covered year, a client with an open job or active recurring rule raises one 'Authorization coverage ending' notification to the staff representative (or the principal), through the existing notification preferences, quiet hours and live authority. Every step is in the client's history; the records are portable and join the signed_documents (authorizations, representative and CAF redacted on client erasure) and structure (transcript requests) classes. **Form preparation (sx-blotter-c38):** staff review the recorded scope, signer authority, representative eligibility and replacement of prior authorizations, then prepare the official January 2021 IRS Form 2848 or 8821 from taxpayer and representative details. Values are flattened before SIGN-002 places the taxpayer signature/date and, for a 2848, the named staff representative's declaration signature/date. More than three matters use a line-3 continuation page. The TIN is kept only in that document, not audit detail or a separate client field. Preparation creates a reviewable signature draft and sends nothing. Staff supply a state agency's own equivalent through SIGN-002. A completed IRS request must match the authorization's form kind before it can be filed. Agency-contact entries name their tax form, and every year in the notice period must be covered; transcript and agency-contact writes recheck the recorded authorization inside the write. A continuing recurrence without an open job alerts the principal. INTEGRATE-006 inherits actual transcript retrieval and its recorded-authorization scope; DUE-002 and NOTICE-001 inherit this scope for future agency-contact doors. IRS submission and CAF acceptance here are practitioner-recorded facts, never automatic transmissions or inferred acceptance.

**WORK-001 — Reusable engagement templates.** A principal or reviewer creates reusable monthly, quarterly or annual templates containing a checklist, document request list and fixed fee. Starting an engagement copies the template into its own period work so staff have concrete tasks and requests. Work types and statuses are WORK-007; task-level owners and dates are WORK-009; the maintained US starter library is WORK-008. **Acceptance evidence:** Through the app or authenticated HTTP doors, create a recurring template, start a client job and inspect copied checklist, requests, recurrence, fee, preparer and reviewer. A preparer cannot create templates.

**WORK-002 — Automatic recurring work and roll forward.** Approved recurrence rules create the next period automatically with assigned staff, fresh requests, dependencies, budget and calculated due dates. Support monthly closes, quarterly payroll/sales tax, annual returns and custom schedules, including fiscal-year ends. Each rule has a creation lead time (how far ahead of a period's start its work is created, set by the firm, for example three months as in Karbon) and an end date. A rule may already hold future periods, whether it generated them or a migration imported and claimed them (MIGRATE-006); a period the rule already holds is never generated again, and the next generated period follows the last held one without a gap. Preview the schedule, pause/skip a period and catch up after downtime without duplicate client-period engagements; historical sign-offs remain immutable. **Acceptance evidence:** Enable monthly and fiscal-year recurrence with a three-month lead time, let scheduled work become due and inspect exactly the periods inside the lead time, each once, with fresh requests. Attach two existing future jobs to a monthly rule and advance the horizon; the rule creates only the following period. Restart the scheduler, pause a client, skip a period and override a due date; no duplicate or silently altered prior job appears. **Semantics (WORK-002):** a principal or reviewer approves one rule per client and template; approving it is the approval. Periods start on the first period's day in the chosen months, which are the template's own monthly, quarterly or annual cadence or a subset of it (custom schedules); a fiscal year is an annual first period in its first month. The end date is the last period's start, inclusive. The lead time is whole months: a period's job is created once the run's UTC calendar date reaches its start less the lead time. Its due date is the period's last day plus the rule's calendar days (a firm rule), or, when the rule names a client obligation, that obligation's calculated working due date for the period (DUE-001, DUE-003), shown in the rule's preview and stored with each job it creates. Budget is the rule's time budget in minutes, copied to each job; staff, fresh document requests and the template's task dependencies (WORK-003) come with each job. The scheduler is an hourly Cron Trigger (minute 17, UTC; `rer dev` runs it; deploys register it) plus Run now; each run creates, in order, every period through the horizon not yet held (generated, claimed or skipped), so restarts repeat nothing and runs after downtime or a pause catch up. A job that already exists for the client, template and period is claimed instead of duplicated; staff may also claim one, and imported future items (MIGRATE-006) must be claimed the same way before that clause ships. Skipping needs a reason. A rule whose people can no longer do the work is held and named in the run log, never reassigned. Created jobs are never changed by a rule: a person overrides a due date on the job, and sign-offs stay immutable.

**WORK-003 — Dependencies and conditional workflow.** Templates define task dependencies, conditional branches, required evidence and preparer/reviewer gates across jobs. Completion events advance only eligible steps, with visible reasons for blocked work; a dependency cycle is rejected and an authorized exception requires a recorded reason. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a close feeding a tax engagement, branch on an organizer answer and complete prerequisite tasks. Inspect automatic advancement and blocked successors; reject a cycle and record an authorized exception without fabricating evidence. **Semantics (WORK-003):** a template task may wait for other tasks of its job, for accepted client documents (its required evidence) and for the same client's prerequisite job from a named template, submitted for review (preparer gate) or signed off (reviewer gate); that prerequisite is the job whose period contains this job's last period day. A task may apply only when a job question has one of the chosen answers: unanswered, it waits; answered otherwise, it does not apply, is not needed for review, and counts as satisfied for tasks waiting on it. Job staff can record workflow questions directly; confirmed PORTAL-004 submissions write their validated bound choices to those same questions, with contact attribution. Drafts and unconfirmed carried values never choose a workflow branch; future answer sources inherit those rules before shipping. Completion events (task done or reopened, document accepted, answer, job submitted, returned or signed off, exception) stamp each gated task that became ready and alert its owner, and clear the stamp when it is blocked again. A cycle among a template's tasks is refused when it is saved; templates are saved as new versions that may wait only on templates that already exist, so cross-job waits cannot form a cycle. The job's reviewer, its manager or the principal may record an exception with a required reason: the task can then be worked, but nothing it waited for is completed, its own required attachment is still required, review still needs every applicable task done and every document accepted, and an unanswered branch question is never waived.

**WORK-004 — Bulk work scheduling and assignment.** Preview and create or reschedule work for a selected client segment in bulk, resolving preparer/reviewer roles, staff eligibility and client-specific exceptions. Changes show impacted jobs and conflicts before approval and preserve existing work and independent review. Until CRM-002 client groups exist, the bulk segment is the clients selected in the batch, with include/exclude per client; once CRM-002 lands, choosing a group pre-selects its clients. Bulk start refuses any self-review assignment, including a principal as both preparer and reviewer. A solo principal starts such a job one at a time, where REVIEW-001’s acknowledged self-review applies. **Acceptance evidence:** Preview quarterly jobs for the clients selected in a batch using per-client include/exclude; once CRM-002 client groups exist, verify choosing a group pre-selects its clients. Override two assignees, exclude one client and commit. Re-submit the same batch and inspect no duplicates, then bulk reassign work while refusing inactive or self-review assignments. Verify bulk start refuses every self-review assignment, including a principal assigned as both preparer and reviewer; verify a solo principal can instead start such a job one at a time with REVIEW-001’s acknowledged self-review.

**WORK-005 — Firm work queues.** Staff see a due-date-ordered work queue with client, period, preparer, reviewer, status and outstanding checklist/document counts. Preparers see their assigned jobs; principals and reviewers see firm work and can open its detail. **Acceptance evidence:** Create two jobs for different preparers, open the work queue as each role and inspect dates, assignees, status and outstanding counts. Directly requesting another preparer's hidden job is refused.

**WORK-006 — Personal plans boards and calendars.** Provide a weekly personal action plan of the person's jobs and tasks (WORK-009), Kanban boards and firm/client calendars filtered by work type, primary status, sub-status, assignee, due date, blocked status and priority. Board columns are the firm's primary statuses, or the selected work type's sub-statuses (WORK-007). Moving a card sets that status on the underlying job, respects workflow and review gates and fires status automations; calendar changes show deadline and capacity consequences. **Acceptance evidence:** Plan a preparer's week from the overdue queue, group a 1040 board by sub-status, move an eligible card and inspect the same job's new status in queue, calendar and client views. A blocked review transition is refused and filters persist after refresh. **Status model (WORK-007, inherited before this ships):** moving a card or planning a job uses WORK-007's moves, sub-status limits and review gates and is recorded in its status history. **Acceptance evidence (WORK-007):** the moved card's change appears in the job's status history. **Semantics (WORK-006):** a person's plan is a Monday-to-Sunday week: the jobs (where they are preparer, reviewer, manager or partner) and their own open tasks they place on its days, each job shown with its status, flags and WORK-007 move control, plus WORK-009's open tasks due in or before the week (or undated) and open jobs due in or before it to plan from; placing work never changes its status. Each person plans their own week; until an admin role exists the principal opens and plans anyone's (pattern 2). Boards, calendars and the queue share filters over the jobs a person may read: work type, stage, sub-status, client, assignee (the job's preparer, reviewer, manager or partner), due dates as an inclusive range, overdue (due before today in UTC and not completed), blocked (open with remaining tasks of which none is ready, each waiting on a WORK-003 dependency or answer, with those reasons shown) and priority (Low, Normal or High, Normal by default, set by the job's people until it is completed). A board has a column per stage, or for one chosen work type a column per stage and each sub-status that type may use (plus In review – partner sign-off when a job is in it); a card move is WORK-007's move, so In review and Completed are reached only by submission and sign-off. The firm calendar shows jobs and their open tasks on their due dates over at most 62 days; the client filter makes it one client's calendar. Moving a job's due date on the calendar is WORK-004's reschedule (principal or reviewer): its preview lists the task dates that follow it, anything that would fall due before today, and each person's estimated demand against available hours (CAPACITY-001) in every week the job's estimated work leaves or enters, and it commits only with that preview's fingerprint. Each person's last board filters (with the column grouping) and calendar filters are kept for them, so a refresh opens the same view. **Automations (AUTOMATE-001, inherited before it ships):** a board card or plan move is a WORK-007 status change recorded in the job's history, so AUTOMATE-001's status triggers fire on it as on any other move; WORK-006 is done for every capability that exists today.

**WORK-007 — Firm work types and status model.** The firm defines work types such as Monthly Bookkeeping, 1040, 1120-S, Payroll Quarterly, Sales Tax, Advisory and internal firm work. Each type has a default template, job roles (for example Manager, Preparer, Reviewer and Partner sign-off), default budget hours, a color and its permitted statuses. Every work item carries exactly one work type and one status. The status is one of six fixed primary stages (Planned, Ready to start, In progress, Waiting, In review, Completed) plus optional firm-defined sub-statuses under each stage, for example "Waiting – on client documents" or "In progress – ready to file". The firm limits each sub-status to selected work types. Statuses drive Kanban columns and personal plans (WORK-006), queue filters and saved views, automation triggers and actions (AUTOMATE-001), client-facing progress labels (PORTAL-003) and status reports (REPORT-001), including counts and time in each status. Entering In review or Completed still requires the REVIEW-001 gates, and no sub-status can bypass them. Every status change records who made it, when, and the old and new status. Renaming a sub-status keeps history. Deleting a sub-status that jobs still use is refused until a previewed bulk reassignment moves those jobs to another permitted status. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a 1040 work type and two sub-statuses under Waiting: "on client documents" and "on 8879 signature". Limit the second to 1040 and confirm it is not offered on a Monthly Bookkeeping job. Move a 1040 job through both sub-statuses on the board. An automation fires once on entering "on 8879 signature". Filter the queue and a saved view by that sub-status, and read a time-in-status report. Moving a job to Completed without review is refused. Deleting a sub-status in use is refused until a previewed bulk reassignment moves its jobs; status history is retained. Import a Karbon work item under MIGRATE-001 and confirm it keeps its work type and status. **Capacity (CAPACITY-001, inherited before this ships):** the capacity view's service filter selects jobs by work type. **Acceptance evidence (CAPACITY-001):** filter the capacity week by the 1040 work type and see only 1040 demand. **Semantics (WORK-007):** until an admin role exists the principal defines work types (name unique ignoring case, optional default template, default budget in minutes applied when a job is started without one, #rrggbb color) and sub-statuses (one stage each, unique by name within it, limited to selected work types or open to every type). Saving a template also creates a work type of the template's name with it as default template; a job carries the work type chosen when it is started, otherwise its template's, and a rolled-forward job keeps its predecessor's. A new job starts Planned; jobs that existed before the status model start In progress, with history beginning at their current stage as of their submission, sign-off or creation. Planned, Ready to start, In progress and Waiting (and their sub-statuses) are set by the job's people while it is open; In review is reached only by submission (or a client's approval that submits, recorded as that approval) and Completed only by sign-off; a return goes to In progress; entering In review or Completed clears the sub-status, and the database refuses any sub-status outside the job's current stage. Each history entry records the old and new stage and sub-status, who and when (UTC); a rename shows the new name throughout history; a deleted sub-status keeps its name in history. Deleting a sub-status that jobs use requires a preview naming the jobs and their target stage (open stages only for an open-stage sub-status, the same stage otherwise) and commits only with that preview's fingerprint, moving the jobs and recording each move. The queue filters by work type, stage and sub-status over the jobs a person may read; time in status runs from each entry to the next (or now), in whole minutes rounded down, with entries, jobs now in it, total and average. Each person keeps private saved views of the queue (work type, stage, sub-status by name). A sub-status may carry a client label: the client link shows it while the job is in that sub-status, otherwise the stage's name (PORTAL-003). **Job roles (WORK-007):** a work type may also need a Manager and a Partner; a job of that type names them when it starts (jobs from recurring rules and bulk scheduling use the template's own type, which needs neither). The partner is an active reviewer or the principal and never the preparer (enforced on every reassignment, offboarding and handover); the reviewer's sign-off records the review and leaves the job In review – partner sign-off, and only the named partner or the principal completes or returns it; a return clears the recorded review. **Inherited before they ship:** AUTOMATE-001 status triggers and set-status actions, WORK-006 plans and boards, REPORT-001 status reports and the MIGRATE-001 Karbon import carry WORK-007's status model in their own text and acceptance; WORK-007 is done for every capability that exists today.

**WORK-008 — Starter US template library.** Blotter maintains a versioned starter library of US templates that a firm can adopt and edit: monthly bookkeeping close, quarterly payroll (941, state withholding and unemployment), sales-tax filing, the 1040, 1120-S, 1065, 1120, 1041 and 990 returns, year-end 1099 and W-2, tax notice response, new-client onboarding and client offboarding. Each template carries a work type and statuses (WORK-007), tasks with relative dates and role assignments (WORK-009), request lists, an organizer (PORTAL-004), budget hours and message templates (MSG-001). Adopting a template copies that version into the firm. Library updates arrive as a previewed diff the firm accepts or ignores change by change, and they never overwrite firm edits or existing jobs. **Acceptance evidence:** In a new US firm, browse the library and adopt the 1040 and monthly close templates. Edit one task and start a job from each, then inspect the copied tasks, requests, relative dates, statuses and messages. Publish a library update, preview its diff, accept one change and reject another. The firm's edited task survives and existing jobs are unchanged. **Semantics (WORK-008):** the maintained native library contains monthly close; quarterly 941, state withholding and unemployment; sales-tax filing; 1040, 1120-S, 1065, 1120, 1041 and 990 returns; year-end 1099 and W-2; notice response; onboarding and offboarding. Each adoption makes a firm template, its own WORK-007 work type with all six stages, WORK-009 role tasks and relative dates, requests, an integer-minute default budget and MSG-001 message copies. Hours are minutes divided by 60, rounded to two decimals for display; planning offsets are whole days from the recorded period start or due date, not statutory calculations. The principal adopts a chosen version, edits tasks, requests and budget, and edits messages through MSG-001. A new job copies the then-current tasks, requests, budget and message text/version; later library changes never mutate those jobs. Authored releases are bundled with the app; a principal can import a reviewed newer release package with its source/change note and author recorded. Imported releases are immutable, never claim agency verification and never change adoptions automatically. An update preview compares the prior adopted release, current firm copy (including MSG-001 edits/deletions) and new release, one task, request, message, budget or description at a time. Each change is accepted or ignored; a conflicting firm edit must be retained, and stale previews are refused. Ignored changes remain firm choices and the reviewed release becomes the next comparison baseline. **PORTAL-004 integration:** every authored library workflow now carries a versioned organizer with conditions and supporting-request bindings; firm question edits and individual release choices follow the same three-way conflict rules, and existing job snapshots stay unchanged. Published packages can bind confirmed organizer choices to WORK-003 workflow questions; those bindings are validated before publication/adoption.

**WORK-009 — Task assignees due dates and instructions.** Each task in a work item can have its own assignee (a named person or a job role), a start and due date relative to the work's start or due date, a time estimate, instructions with an SOP link, a required attachment and a client-facing flag (PORTAL-003). Completing a task records who completed it and when. Changing the person in a job role re-routes that role's open tasks, while completed tasks keep their completer. Personal plans (WORK-006) list the person's tasks as well as their jobs. Until WORK-007 adds firm job roles, a job's roles are Preparer, Reviewer and Manager, and the Manager is the job's reviewer unless someone is named when the job starts. The work's start date is its period start. Task start and due dates are whole days before or after the work's start or due date and are computed when read, so open tasks follow every change to the job's due date or people; completing a task records its completer and time and keeps the owner and dates it had then. A task may be assigned by name to any active practice member or the principal; that person can then read the job and act on their own tasks (ACCESS-001). A task that needs an attachment completes only with one. A client-facing task shows only its name, due date and done state on the client's link; PORTAL-003 inherits client-facing tasks before it ships. Until WORK-006 ships, a person's weekly plan for a Monday-to-Sunday week lists their open tasks due in or before that week or with no due date, and their open jobs as preparer, reviewer or manager due in or before it; WORK-006 inherits tasks before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a template with three tasks due 10, 5 and 2 days before the work's due date, assigned to Preparer, Manager and a named person. Start a job and inspect the computed task dates and owners. Move the work's due date and see the open task dates follow. Change the job's Preparer and confirm the open tasks move to the new person, while a completed task keeps its original completer and time. Open a task's SOP link, and see the tasks in the new owner's weekly plan.

**DUE-001 — Sourced US obligations and extensions.** Provide maintained federal and firm-selected state deadline templates for 1040, 1120-S, 1065, 941 and sales tax, with entity/period/fiscal-year applicability, weekend/holiday rules, state/local frequency and jurisdiction-specific extensions or disaster relief. Import IRS and state revenue calendar updates with source URL, effective date and rule version. A firm approves applicable rules and material changes, sees recalculated due dates and can override with reason; original, extended and internal dates remain distinct. Extension work stays open until the tax authority supplies filing evidence. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure all five obligation types for clients in two states and different fiscal years. Calculate a weekend/holiday case, import a source revision and preview affected jobs before approval. Record an extension and override; verify separate original/extended/internal dates, preserved provenance and no claim of filing from a checklist. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping. **Semantics (DUE-001):** Blotter ships a maintained catalog (release 2026.1, effective 1 January 2026) of sourced rules, each with its agency source URL, version and effective date: federal 1040 (15th day of the 4th month after the tax year; Form 4868 extension to the 15th day of the 10th), 1120-S and 1065 (15th day of the 3rd month; Form 7004 to the 15th day of the 9th), 941 (last day of the month after each calendar quarter) and state sales tax (California CDTFA quarterly: last day of the month after the quarter; Texas Comptroller monthly: the 20th of the month after). Blotter does not fetch agency sites: a person imports each IRS or state revision. Until an admin role exists the principal approves each catalog rule for the firm (approving a state's rule selects that state; pattern 2), and a principal or reviewer configures a client obligation: one approved rule with the client's two-letter state, fiscal-year-end month (calendar-year rules always December) and internal lead days (0–90); a rule applies only to its entity types (individual, business, trust) and a state rule only to its own state. A job started from an obligation, rolled forward from such a job, or created by a WORK-002 rule that names one takes its period from its template's cadence (starting on the first of a month; an annual period ends in the fiscal-year-end month, quarterly periods are the tax year's quarters) and keeps these dates apart: the statutory date; the original due date, which is the statutory date moved to the next business day past Saturdays, Sundays and federal legal holidays (5 U.S.C. 6103; a Saturday holiday is observed the Friday before, a Sunday one the Monday after) and, for federal rules, DC Emancipation Day (16 April, observed; 26 U.S.C. 7503), with the reason recorded; the extended due date (shifted the same way), which applies once a person on the job records the extension request, or at once for an automatic extension; a relief date from an approved disaster postponement whose jurisdiction, states, rules and inclusive window cover the original or extended date; the internal target (that external date less the obligation's lead days, moved earlier to a business day); and any override. The job's working due date is the override, else the relief, extended or original date; an override needs a principal or reviewer and a reason and never changes a calculated date. A source revision is a JSON document with version, effective date, https source and changed rules (keeping each rule's key and jurisdiction) or relief windows; only the principal previews and approves it. The preview lists every job not yet signed off whose dates or rule version change, and approval commits only with that preview's fingerprint, approving the revision's rules and recalculating those jobs; a job whose working date was set by hand (an override, or a WORK-004/WORK-006 move) keeps it while its calculated dates update. Filing is never inferred from a checklist, review, sign-off or status: only a recorded agency acknowledgment (submission ID, accepted date and an acknowledgment file on the job, labeled practitioner-recorded until INTEGRATE-008 supplies stack status) marks a return filed, and a job whose extension was recorded cannot be signed off until it exists (pattern 3). Agent keys cannot approve rules or revisions. Rules, revisions, relief, obligations and job dates are carried by native archives and move with a merged client (CRM-004); the acknowledgment file follows file erasure and stale-archive fencing.

**DUE-002 — Tax notices and resolution work.** Capture a federal/state notice with its source file, agency, tax period, response date, assigned practitioner, authorization and resolution plan. Track research, client questions, agency contact, response submission and follow-up until an acknowledged resolution or documented exception; link transcripts and filing receipts without treating them as tax advice. A notice opens from a document already filed on a job, such as a client upload, and its response date is the one printed on the notice, recorded and then verified by a person; Blotter never computes it. Until AUTHZ-001 tracks Forms 2848 and 8821, the authorization is the reference staff record on the notice; until INTEGRATE-006 retrieves transcripts, a transcript is a file staff attach, and AUTHZ-001 and INTEGRATE-006 inherit these links before they ship. The timeline is append-only. A notice closes only as resolved, backed by an evidence file on an agency contact, transcript, receipt or accepted response and with no failed response after the last accepted one, or as a documented exception with its reason; the assigned practitioner, a reviewer or the principal closes it. **Acceptance evidence:** Open a notice from a client upload, verify the response deadline, assign a practitioner, link an authorized transcript and response receipt, and schedule follow-up. A failed response stays open; closing requires evidence and a recorded outcome.

**DUE-003 — Wider US obligation catalog and firm defined deadlines.** Beyond DUE-001's five obligation types, Blotter maintains sourced deadline templates for Forms 1120, 1041, the 990 series, 940, W-2/W-3, 1099-NEC/1099-MISC, 1040-ES and 1120-W estimated payments, state withholding and unemployment returns, state annual reports and franchise taxes, and FinCEN 114 (FBAR) with its automatic extension. A firm can also define its own obligations: a fixed date, N days after period end, or the nth weekday of a month, each with a recorded source or a firm-defined label. The same approval, override, weekend/holiday and provenance rules as DUE-001 apply. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure 1040-ES quarterly estimates including a weekend shift, the January 31 W-2 and 1099-NEC deadlines, an FBAR with its automatic October extension, and a firm rule of 15 days after month end. Inspect the calculated dates and their sources. Import a source revision and preview the affected jobs before approving it. The firm rule shows as firm-defined rather than as an agency deadline. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping. **Semantics (DUE-003):** the 2026.1 catalog adds 1120 (15th day of the 4th month; Form 7004 to the 15th day of the 10th; a fiscal year ending 30 June that starts before 1 January 2026 uses the 15th day of the 3rd month, extended to the 15th day of the 10th), 1041 (15th day of the 4th; Form 7004 to the last day of the 9th), the 990 series (15th day of the 5th; Form 8868 to the 15th day of the 11th), 940, W-2/W-3 and 1099-NEC (31 January after the calendar year), 1099-MISC filed electronically (31 March), 1040-ES (15 April, 15 June, 15 September and 15 January: the 15th day of the tax year's 4th, 6th, 9th and 13th months, one per quarter period) and 1120-W (15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th and 12th months), FinCEN 114 (15 April with the automatic extension to 15 October, labeled automatic), state withholding and unemployment returns (California EDD DE 9 and Texas TWC C-3: last day of the month after the quarter), and state franchise taxes and annual reports (Texas franchise report 15 May, extension to 15 August on request; Delaware corporation annual report and franchise tax 1 March). Only the principal defines a firm rule (defining it approves it; pattern 2): a fixed month and day (the first such date after the period ends), a number of calendar days after the period ends, or the nth (1–5, or last) weekday of the month a chosen number of months after the period-end month. It carries an optional source or label (default "Firm-defined") and shows as a firm-defined deadline, never as an agency deadline, with no source URL; DUE-001's holiday shift (federal legal holidays, without DC Emancipation Day), obligation, override, revision and provenance rules apply to it unchanged.

**RESOLVE-001 — Transcript analysis and resolution cases.** From authorized IRS account and wage-and-income transcripts (INTEGRATE-006), Blotter builds a per-year view for each client. It shows the assessed balance and the accrued penalties and interest as of the transcript date, each transaction code with a plain explanation, unfiled years, the collection statute expiration date (CSED) for each assessment, refund statute dates, and hold, lien or levy indicators. Each figure links to its transcript line. When a new pull changes a year, the change is flagged and routed to the assigned practitioner as notice or resolution work (DUE-002). Financial information for Forms 433-A and 433-F is collected through a PORTAL-004 organizer. Derived figures are labeled with their transcript date and are never presented as advice; the practitioner chooses the resolution path. **Acceptance evidence:** Load authorized account transcripts for four years, including one unfiled year. Inspect each year's balance, codes, CSED and unfiled flag against the source lines. Pull again with a new transaction code and see a change alert routed to the practitioner. Collect 433-A data through an organizer and inspect it on the case. No resolution recommendation is made without the practitioner's decision. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping. **Inherited PORTAL-004:** before its 433-A/F case organizers ship, they retain versioned conditional/required questions, authorized per-question contact responsibility, supporting uploads, save/resume, explicitly confirmed prior-period carry, immutable submitted corrections and staff completeness/review; only submitted current confirmations drive case/workflow choices.

**MAIL-001 — Gmail and Microsoft 365 shared inbox.** Connect Gmail/Google Workspace and Microsoft 365/Exchange mailboxes with scoped OAuth, shared/delegated mailbox access and visible sync health. Triage threads into clients and engagements, assign email as work, comment internally, send/reply with the authorized identity using firm or personal templates (MSG-001) and file attachments against the correct job. Colleague visibility follows MAIL-002; snooze, scheduled send and no-reply follow-up are MAIL-003. Preserve message/thread identity, timestamps and authors, prevent duplicate sends/imports, and quarantine ambiguous client matches. Revocation stops access and surfaces unsynced work. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect a real authorized Google mailbox and Microsoft shared mailbox, receive and reply to client threads, delegate one as a job and file an attachment. Send the same event twice, introduce an ambiguous sender and revoke access; inspect one copy, explicit triage and actionable sync failure. **Time suggestions (TIME-001, inherited before this ships):** a person's connected-mailbox activity becomes a TIME-001 activity-suggestion source only with that person's separate consent for mail, given and withdrawn by them; each suggestion links the message it came from, and nothing is recorded until they approve it. **Acceptance evidence (TIME-001):** with mail consent, a sent client reply suggests time on its job linking that message; without it, or after withdrawal, mail suggests nothing. **Offboarding (ACCESS-006, inherited before this ships):** a departing staff member's connected mailbox, triaged threads and mailbox grants appear in the offboarding preview; Each factor comes with ten one-time recovery codes; a recovery code opens only the setup of a new factor, which replaces the lost one, issues new codes and ends the account's other sessions, and the principal can reset a factor with a recorded reason, ending every session. Five wrong codes in 15 minutes lock the account for 15 minutes. **PORTAL-003 — Client progress secure chat and to dos.** Clients see engagement milestones, next action, outstanding requests and review/completion progress, and exchange secure messages or to-dos attached to the right engagement. Staff set to-dos for the client (with an optional due date) and own them; the client completes one with an optional reply, which alerts its owner and completes no request, task or other to-do. Staff messages appear on the link only: no email is sent for them. A client may hold at most 20 unanswered questions per job; the client's writes are same-origin only and refused once the link is replaced, expired or the job is signed off. Questions and to-dos are CRM-003 unresolved items that change hands like any other and move with ACCESS-006 offboarding; every question, answer, message, to-do and completion is in the client history. **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** Progress links never carry marketing.

Completion preserves the exact original behind the usual permission-checked file door and marks the request received for staff acceptance. Corrections retain every prior original and the preceding exact DOC-002 contact grants, never its share tokens, and start unreviewed. Notes name a page and exact version; review records status, author and time without altering original bytes. Search covers names, sources, authors, period, annotations and review metadata; SEARCH-001 also indexes supported PDF text from the real bytes. Final chunks, versions, annotations and grants are portable; pending chunks and bearer credentials are excluded. Existing file erasure removes final chunks and pending copies under the stale-restore fence. **SEARCH-001 — Firm wide search.** One search covers clients, contacts, work items, tasks, emails, portal messages, notes, documents (by name and extracted text) and invoices. Results can be filtered by type, are ordered by relevance and recency, tolerate typos and open from the keyboard. They include only what the searcher may see under ACCESS-002 and MAIL-002. Extracted text is read from plain-text and CSV files and from the strings a PDF's content streams (uncompressed or FlateDecode) show; scanned images and other encodings yield none (nothing is guessed). A document's text is extracted on the first search after upload and kept; erasing the file's bytes deletes it, and it is left out of archives. Query and record text are split into words (case and accents ignored). Every query word must match a word of the result exactly (3), as a prefix (2) or within one typo for words of 4 to 7 letters, two for 8 or more (1, insertions, deletions, substitutions and transpositions); a match in the result's own name counts double, and the whole query appearing as a phrase adds 5. Results are ordered by that score, then most recent first (the record's latest activity: done, answered, uploaded, posted or created), at most 50, optionally filtered to one type, and each carries the door that opens it (the client's history, the job, the discussion, or the file download); in the app "/" focuses the box, arrow keys move and Enter opens the chosen result.
