**CAPACITY-001 — Workload capacity and coverage.** Plan staff hours by week, skill, service, availability, leave and non-client commitments against estimated remaining work and review demand. Show overload, unscheduled work and deadline conflicts across the firm with drill-down to jobs; distinguish estimates from actual time. **Acceptance evidence:** Load a tax-season week with preparer/reviewer budgets, scheduled leave and a client meeting. Inspect available hours, overloaded staff and affected jobs; adjust an estimate and confirm totals and conflict explanations update. **Semantics (CAPACITY-001):** a capacity week runs Monday to Sunday (UTC dates). Until an admin role exists the principal sets each person's weekly hours (in minutes; 40 hours when unset, shown as a default) and skills, and schedules leave (whole weekdays at a fifth of the weekly hours each), client meetings and internal commitments (minutes on each weekday from one date to another, a meeting optionally linked to its job); only weekdays Monday to Friday count. Available = weekly hours less leave and commitments in the week, never below zero. Demand is estimated remaining work: the estimates of open, applicable tasks a person owns (WORK-009 owner resolution) whose due date (the task's, else the job's) falls in the week, plus the review estimate of each job they review that is not signed off and falls due in the week. Actual time is the person's recorded time in the week, and per job their total time on it, shown beside the estimates and never subtracted from them. A person is overloaded when demand exceeds available. Open tasks or reviews due in the week without an estimate are unscheduled; open tasks due before the week are listed as past due; neither counts toward demand. A deadline conflict is a job due in the week that is not signed off, with one explanation for each of its people who is overloaded or on leave between the week's start and its due date, and for each unscheduled item on it. The view filters by skill (people who have it) and service (the job's work type, WORK-007) and drills down to each job; reviewers and the principal see the whole firm, a preparer sees only themselves. The job's people (or a reviewer or the principal) adjust an open task's estimate or the job's review estimate; every change is audited. CAPACITY-002 and CAPACITY-003 build on this model.

**CAPACITY-002 — Reassignment and dependency aware scheduling.** Reassign and reschedule work when staff are absent or overloaded, proposing eligible coverage with client authority, skills, remaining capacity, dependency order and independent reviewer constraints. Preview notifications and affected deadlines; a manager approves the plan and owns unresolved conflicts. **Acceptance evidence:** Remove an assigned preparer for leave, preview alternate staffing and move a dependent job chain. Approve the feasible changes, refuse an ineligible/self-review assignment and inspect new owners, notifications and unresolved deadline conflicts. **Semantics (CAPACITY-002):** a manager is a reviewer or the principal (the people who reschedule under WORK-004); they plan cover for a person on leave or over capacity between two dates (at most 92 days apart). The plan takes the open jobs that person prepares, and the jobs not yet completed that they review, falling due from the first date through 14 days after the last, ordered so each job comes after the planned jobs it waits for (WORK-003) and otherwise by due date. For each role the person holds it proposes an eligible colleague (preparer: an active preparer, reviewer or the principal; reviewer: an active reviewer or the principal) who is not the person, never reviews their own work, is not the job's partner as preparer, is not on CAPACITY-001 leave on the due date and still has the job's estimated minutes free that week (available less demand less the plan's earlier moves); the colleague covering a job's prerequisite comes first, then one with the job's work type among their skills, then the most free minutes, then email order. A manager may name the preparer or reviewer, move a due date (with where it comes from) or leave a job out; a named person who is ineligible, would review their own work or lacks the capacity, or a prerequisite that would fall due after the job waiting for it, refuses the plan until changed. The preview lists every line, the notifications and the unresolved conflicts (no eligible colleague free); approval needs the preview's fingerprint, applies every feasible line in one batch (role tasks follow, WORK-009), sends each notice in-app and by email with its delivery recorded, and records each conflict owned by the approving manager in the plan and among the client's unresolved items (CRM-003), where it can be handed on and is closed with a resolution note by its owner or the principal. **Client authority (ACCESS-002, inherited before it ships):** until client grants exist every active member may work any client; when ACCESS-002 adds client and team grants, a proposed or named colleague must hold the client's grant. CAPACITY-002 is done for every capability that exists today.

**CAPACITY-003 — Capacity forecasts and hiring plans.** Forecast future workload from approved recurring engagements, historical completion/time, pipeline and seasonality, with visible assumptions and confidence ranges. Compare staffing, hiring or service-change scenarios without altering actual assignments or promised deadlines. **Acceptance evidence:** Project the next tax season from recurring work and prior actuals, add a hypothetical hire and lost client, and compare demand/capacity by skill. Inspect each week's forecast as a range with its stated confidence level, and confirm a client with no prior actuals widens the range and is named as the reason. Trace estimates to sources and save a scenario without changing live work. **Semantics (CAPACITY-003):** a manager (a reviewer or the principal, as in CAPACITY-002; a preparer sees only their own capacity under CAPACITY-001) forecasts 1 to 53 Monday-to-Sunday weeks (UTC dates) from a Monday. Demand is the periods of active, approved recurring rules (WORK-002) whose due date (the period's last day plus the rule's days) falls in a week, counted in that week; paused rules, skipped periods and periods whose job is already signed off are left out, and one-off jobs are not forecast. A period's time traces to its source: the client's prior actuals for that template, which are the recorded time (TIME-001) on its signed-off jobs of earlier periods (a signed-off job with no recorded time is not one), using only periods starting in the same calendar month when there are any (seasonality); the estimate is their mean rounded to the minute, and the range runs from 90% of the smallest (rounded down) to 110% of the largest (rounded up). Without prior actuals the period uses the rule's time budget, else the work type's budget, else the sum of the template's task estimates, with a range from 50% to 150% of it (rounded to the minute), and the reason names the client; with none of these its estimate is zero and the reason says so. Each week states its confidence: high when every period due in it rests on at least three prior actuals, medium when each rests on at least one, low when any rests on none (each such reason listed). Capacity is each active person's weekly hours less leave and commitments on the week's weekdays (CAPACITY-001); by skill, a person counts in full under each of their skills, and demand counts under the skill named like its work type (lower case); a skill is short by its demand's high end less its capacity. A scenario adds hypothetical hires (weekly minutes and skills from a start date), changes a person's weekly hours from a date (zero for a departure), drops lost clients' periods (listed as left out) and scales a work type's time to a percentage (0 drops the service); it is compared week by week and by skill with the baseline. Forecasting computes from live records and stores nothing; saving a scenario stores only its name, window and changes (audited) and changes no job, rule, assignment, estimate, due date or capacity row; reopening it recomputes from current records. **Pipeline (CRM-005):** each open prospect’s requested service contributes its own visible unweighted assumption that the prospect wins, with current stage, source, owner and whole-prospect annual fee in its stored currency. An exact case-insensitive service/work-type name match is the default; the manager may choose another work type or leave the service unestimated. Its first assumed work target defaults to the forecast start or is selected per service; demand repeats at the selected template’s monthly/quarterly/annual cadence through the window, or occurs once without a template. Each engagement uses the same no-actuals estimate chain as recurring work (work-type budget, else template task estimates), with a 50%–150% range rounded to the minute. Missing matches or budgets contribute zero explicitly labeled unestimated, with a named low-confidence reason. Pipeline demand counts in weekly and skill totals in baseline and scenarios; service percentage changes scale it too. Fees never become hours. Won and lost prospects are excluded. These assumptions create no assignments, signed scope or promised deadlines. Saved scenarios retain the selected work type and first target and recompute from current records. CAPACITY-003 is done for every capability that exists today.

**TIME-001 — Time budgets and activity suggestions.** Record time against client/job/task with manual entry and timers, billable status and snapshotted rate; compare actual hours/cost with approved budgets. Suggest missing entries from consented work/email/calendar activity with source links, never silently creating billable time. Corrections retain authorship and respect locks. **Acceptance evidence:** Record time, change the rate and inspect unchanged prior amounts and budget variance. Stop/restart a timer, reject one activity suggestion and approve another; verify only approved minutes enter WIP and unauthorized edits are refused. **Timers and budgets (implemented subset):** a person runs at most one timer, kept by the server so it continues across restarts and devices; stopping it records one time entry through the manual-entry path (rate in force snapshotted, closed periods refused) for the elapsed time rounded up to the next whole minute (at least 1, at most 1440), dated the UTC day the timer started, and a discarded timer records nothing. A job's budget is the minutes approved by the reviewer or principal who starts it, or by its recurrence rule (WORK-002); actual is every recorded entry in any review state plus adjustments, at their snapshotted amounts, and variance is actual minus budget. **Billable status (implemented subset):** each time entry is billable or not, chosen by the person when they record it by hand or start a timer (billable unless they choose otherwise), and a TIME-002 correction keeps the returned entry's status unless the person changes it. A non-billable entry keeps its snapshotted rate and amount and counts in the job's actual time, cost and variance, but neither it nor any adjustment to it is ever ready to bill: it stays out of WIP, is refused in a billing export and stays out of the job's margin (TIME-004). **Semantics (TIME-001):** a time entry or timer names its job, and so its client, and optionally one of that job's checklist tasks; a correction keeps the task unless the person changes it. **Activity suggestions:** consent is per person, off by default, given and withdrawn only by that person on their Jobs screen. While it is on, that person's own audited work actions on jobs they can record time on (completing a checklist task, accepting or returning a document, opening, replying to or requesting a correction in a discussion, any tax-notice timeline action, discarding a timer) taken at or after the moment of consent suggest one entry per job and UTC day on which they recorded no time of their own on that job; each suggestion lists and links its source actions. Only that person sees, approves or rejects their suggestions: approval needs the minutes and an explicit billable choice and records the entry through the manual-entry path (rate in force on that day snapshotted, closed periods refused); rejection records nothing; each decision is kept once with its source action ids. Approved suggestions are ordinary time, so they reach WIP only once approved on a timesheet (TIME-002) and only if billable. Withdrawing consent removes every pending suggestion, and consenting again never uses earlier actions. Email and calendar activity are not sources until MAIL-001 and INTEGRATE-005 ship, each with its own per-source consent (written into those clauses).

**TIME-002 — Timesheet approval and period locks.** Staff submit timesheets to managers, who approve or return entries with reasons. Closing a billing period locks approved time; corrections use an authorized adjustment that preserves the original. Invoice/export reservations prevent the same work being billed twice. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit a weekly timesheet, return and correct one entry, approve it and close the period. Attempt direct edits and duplicate billing, then post an authorized adjustment and inspect its history.

**TIME-003 — Billing rates and rate cards.** Billing rates are set by staff member, role and service or work type, with client-specific overrides and effective dates. The precedence is client and service, then client, then service, then staff member, then role. Role is the person's practice role (principal, reviewer or preparer). Service rates may target a WORK-007 work type or the engagement template the job was started from. Within either service scope (service or client and service), a matching work-type card takes precedence over template cards, then the latest effective date and creation order resolve cards for that target. Template cards continue to apply to jobs started from that template when no work-type card in that scope is in force; work types without a default template may have their own rates. Each time entry snapshots the rate it resolved and where that rate came from. A rate change takes effect from its date and never rewrites past entries. **Acceptance evidence:** Set rates for a practice role, a staff member, a 1040 service, a client and that client plus service. Record time with only the role matching, then with staff, service, client and client-plus-service rates also matching in turn; inspect each entry's resolved rate and source to prove every precedence level: client and service, client, service, staff member, role. Verify role means principal, reviewer or preparer. Start two jobs with distinct work types sharing a template and inspect their distinct service rates; a type without a default template also accepts its own rate. Verify client overrides, work-type versus template specificity, effective dates and recorded snapshots through archive restore. Change the staff rate effective next month and confirm past entries are unchanged.

**TIME-004 — Expenses and disbursements.** Record billable and non-billable expenses (filing fees, postage, mileage at the firm-set rate, software pass-throughs) against a client and work item. Each expense can carry a receipt, a markup and an approval, and approved billable expenses become BILL-002 invoice lines. Staff reimbursements are kept separate from client charges, and expenses count in WIP and profitability (BILL-003). Amounts are integer cents: a markup is a whole percent from 0 to 100 of cost, a billable expense charges its cost plus the markup rounded half up to the cent, and a non-billable expense charges nothing; mileage is miles to one decimal place at the firm's cents-per-mile rate in force on the expense date, rounded half up. A reviewer or the principal approves or rejects an expense, nobody but the principal approves their own, and an expense dated in a closed billing period (TIME-002) cannot be recorded. Staff-paid expenses are owed back to that person at cost, and the principal records each reimbursement. Until BILL-002 issues invoice documents, an expense's invoice line is its line in the reviewed billing export, reserved once; BILL-002 inherits approved billable expenses as invoice lines before it ships. Until BILL-003 ships, WIP is the value of everything ready to bill, and a job's profitability is its margin before staff cost: fixed fee, approved billable time (TIME-001) and its adjustments and approved billable expense charges, less the cost of every approved expense, billable or not; BILL-003 keeps expenses in its WIP and profitability. **Acceptance evidence:** Record a state filing fee with a receipt and a 10% markup, approve it, invoice it and inspect the invoice line and WIP. A non-billable expense stays off the invoice and appears in profitability. An unapproved expense cannot be invoiced.

**BILL-001 — Reviewed immutable billing exports.** Reviewers prepare time/fixed-fee CSV drafts with snapshotted sources. The principal approves once with a note; the approved bytes and digest remain unchanged and each source belongs to one live export. Draft voiding releases reservations; CSV cells neutralize spreadsheet formulas and preserve source currency. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a mixed time/fixed-fee export, reject source reuse and non-owner approval, approve as principal and download twice. Verify identical CSV bytes, source locks, formula-safe cells and a voided draft's released sources. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Approved exports stay immutable; only ERASURE-002's confirmed expiry removes their bytes, keeping number, totals, revision and SHA-256.

**BILL-002 — Invoices retainers and recurring fees.** Create numbered USD invoices from approved time, fixed scope, milestones or recurring retainers; separate fee entitlement from job completion. Preview invoice lines, terms, authorized sales-tax treatment, credits and client recipients, then approve and deliver PDF/portal invoices. Retainer deposits, credits, price changes, cancellation and prorations remain traceable. Select exactly one invoice authority: Blotter, QuickBooks Online or Xero; schedule generation is idempotent. **Acceptance evidence:** Bill a fixed engagement and hourly extra, start a monthly retainer, apply a deposit and preview a fee amendment. Approve/deliver invoices, repeat the schedule event and inspect one invoice per entitlement with USD totals and retained source links. **Engagement history (CRM-003, inherited before this ships):** issued, sent and voided invoices appear in the client's history with author, time and source link, visible only to those who may read the job, and any unresolved item they create names an owner, next action and due condition. **Acceptance evidence (CRM-003):** an issued invoice appears in the client history linked to its source time and fees. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, BILL-002 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026). **Native semantics (sx-blotter-c36/c37, 22 Oct; approved with change by ct, batch 11 H):** The principal selects the sole invoice authority; the principal or an ACCESS-002 financial-authority holder (for the clients the holder holds) authorizes independent fixed/milestone/explicit-proration entitlements, records supplied deposit/credit evidence and tax treatment, approves numbered USD PDF snapshots and delivers them to an authorized billing contact. Approved time, adjustments and expenses share source reservations with reviewed exports; a numbered document never releases its source links. No taxability, bank settlement, charge or automatic proration is inferred. Monthly rules approved by the principal or a financial-authority holder create one draft per rule/month; issue and send are separate person actions unless a holder's recorded automatic-issue consent covers the rule revision (below); price changes and cancellation apply from the reviewed future month while existing entitlement prices remain. An explicit recorded credit allocation changes the current balance, never the issued PDF. Invoice links are contact/revision-bound, expire after 30 days, expose only their invoice and recheck live billing/portal/email authority. Unresolved sends are held for provider-evidence reconciliation without replay. Restored rules are paused and old invoice links revoked. Issued/sent/voided history links to its source job; open balances name an owner, next action and due date. Native invoice search and merge/undo preserve immutable document bytes and sources. Existing performance reports project the selected job cohort’s native invoices, retainers, supplied credits and open USD receivables from live sources, with job/document/source links, generation time and the same values in CSV/PDF; they never label supplied credit evidence as provider settlement. Each report download records its client scope and named downloader for erasure receipts. Invoices, credits, rules and deliveries join ERASURE-002 billing/link classes, holds, counts, receipt and journal fence; open invoice balances and unapplied deposits/credits refuse whole-client erasure and billing expiry. Erased-client invoice identities are absent from normal billing lists and use opaque expiry labels; explicit retained detail/PDF reads require the principal and are audited. Retention clocks use issue and later void/credit/allocation dates in the firm timezone; expiry requires principal confirmation and preserves amounts, number, attribution and SHA-256. INTEGRATE-001 inherits QBO/Xero authority selection and reconciliation before those connectors ship; unavailable external authorities refuse. PAY-001 inherits actual settlement evidence and balances before collections ship. AUTOMATE-001 inherits invoice creation as an additional action before it is exposed; current invoice schedules create approved-rule drafts and, within a recorded consent, issue and send them.

**Ruled (ct 22 Oct):** the principal or an ACCESS-002 financial-authority holder prepares, issues, sends and voids. Selecting the invoice authority and confirming retention expiry stay principal-only. A holder may enable automatic issue and send for one rule revision. The consent records a per-invoice USD cap, the recipient and a reason, and it is audited. Each run rechecks the consenter's live authority, the rule's terms and the recipient's billing role and email or portal consent. A run issues and sends only within the cap and with no exception. Otherwise it leaves a draft with a named exception. The invoice states 'auto-issued under rule revision N'. Delivery may be by email PDF to a billing contact without portal access. A restore brings rules back paused and without consent. **Semantic implemented (sx-blotter-c37):** the consent is one record on the rule: the rule revision the holder reviewed (any amendment, pause or reactivation is a new revision and ends it), the cap, one recipient contact and a reason; recording it is audited and needs step-up, and it never travels in an archive. Each hourly run rechecks that the revision is unchanged, that the consenter is still the principal or a financial-authority holder holding the client, that the invoice recipient is the consented contact with a billing role and email consent (portal access is not needed), and that the invoice total is within the cap. With no exception it issues the numbered PDF under the consenter's authority (the PDF reads 'This invoice was auto-issued under rule revision N') and sends it once; otherwise the invoice stays a draft carrying the named exception and nothing is sent, and a held send or exception is never retried by a later run. A contact without portal access receives the PDF by email alone: no invoice link is mailed and the stored link is born revoked. AUTOMATE-001 inherits automatic issue only through this consent.

**PAY-001 — Card ACH and authorized collections.** Collect invoices by card and US ACH through Stripe, with saved-method mandates and explicit authorization for recurring or due-date automatic collection. Show fees in USD, payment terms and ACH pending/settled/returned states; distinguish provider acceptance from settlement. Verify webhook signatures, deduplicate events, reconcile partial payments, refunds, disputes and returns, and own failed-payment follow-up. Provider onboarding, US bank access and saved-method/auto-pay migration from Karbon Payments, TaxDome Payments, Canopy Payments and Financial Cents (MIGRATE-007) are engineering obligations; a method or authorization that cannot move becomes a tracked client reauthorization, and no client is charged automatically without a valid mandate. **Acceptance evidence:** Pay a real authorized low-value invoice by card and ACH, authorize a recurring mandate and inspect provider receipts and ledger reconciliation. At the provider test edge exercise duplicate/out-of-order events, ACH return, partial payment, refund and failed collection; revoke the mandate and verify no later debit. **Engagement history (CRM-003, inherited before this ships):** payments, failures and refunds appear in the client's history with author, time and source link, visible only to those who may read the job, and any unresolved item they create (a failed payment) names an owner, next action and due condition. **Acceptance evidence (CRM-003):** trace a request from email through upload and review to its payment in the client history. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, PAY-001 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026).

**Implemented PAY-001 subset (26 October 2026):** See `STRIPE.md` for the exact adopted invoice-bounded consent, provider reconciliation, retained records and inactive restore semantics. Recurring collection and incumbent migration remain unbuilt and no automatic retry is authorized. PAY-002, BILL-005, MIGRATE-007, NOTIFY-001 and ERASURE-002 retain their named obligations.

**PAY-002 — Payment plans and client payment self service.** In the portal, clients see open invoices, statements and payment history. They can pay several invoices in one payment, save or remove payment methods, set up auto-pay, and accept a firm-offered installment plan with an amount, a schedule and a mandate. Scheduled charges run only under explicit authorization, with a reminder before each debit. A missed or returned installment creates owned follow-up instead of an unauthorized retry. **Acceptance evidence:** A client pays two invoices in one card payment, and the payment is allocated correctly. The client accepts a three-installment ACH plan; the second installment is returned, which creates owned follow-up with no retry outside the authorized policy. After the client removes a saved card, a later auto-pay is refused. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, PAY-002 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026).

**BILL-003 — WIP receivables realization and profitability.** Report unbilled WIP, earned/deferred retainers, aged receivables, collection follow-up (reminders and statements under BILL-004), credits, write-ups/downs, billed-versus-recorded realization, utilization and client/job/service profitability using approved time, cost and invoice/payment sources. Drill into calculation inputs, exclude duplicate exports and keep uncollected, settled and written-off amounts distinct. Partners approve credits, write-offs and collection messages. **Acceptance evidence:** Run WIP, aging and profitability for a client with hourly work, fixed fees, a retainer, partial payment and credit. Reconcile totals to approved sources and provider state, approve a write-off and inspect the changed period report without rewriting historical invoices. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping. **Implemented native slice (BILL-003):** the performance report groups its selected jobs by client and service/work type, separately for each stored currency. The inclusive period-start cohort and existing client/service/assignee filters apply before grouping. Totals sum approved billable time and adjustments, earned fixed fees, approved expense charges and costs, margin before staff cost, unreserved ready-to-bill WIP and approved export snapshots. Draft reservations remove WIP but never count as approved exports; voiding restores that WIP. Each group links to its source jobs and their calculation inputs. **Implemented native completion (sx-blotter-c40, 22 Oct):** ready-to-bill WIP excludes every source a billing export or an invoice (draft or issued) has reserved; voiding a draft restores it. An issued non-void invoice's open balance is its gross less applied credits and approved write-offs; reminders, statements, the portal and erasure blockers read that one balance. The report adds, for the same period-start cohort and filters, receivables aged by whole days past the due date at the report's firm-local date (current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, over 90); retainer invoices earned (billing month already begun) or deferred (billed for a later month); and per client, service and job: recorded value (approved time, fee and expense lines on issued invoices), write-ups and write-downs (the adjustment lines), billed, billed-against-recorded realization, collected (recorded deposits applied), credits applied, written off, uncollected, invoiced expense cost, staff cost and profit, with each client's unbilled WIP beside them; collected, credited, written-off and uncollected are never merged. Under Blotter as the invoice authority the provider state of money is the practitioner-recorded deposit receipt references and credits; PAY-001 and any QuickBooks or Xero authority inherit the obligation to add their provider payment, refund, return and dispute states to the same figures when they ship. A write-off is approved by the principal or a financial-authority holder in a native person session (as for credits, ct 22 Oct), for a stated USD amount of an issued invoice's open balance with a reason; it is audited, immutable, refused above the balance, and never rewrites the issued invoice, its PDF or its totals: only the balance, the reports and statements dated after it change. Staff cost is the principal-recorded hourly cost rate in force on the entry date times the minutes of invoiced time and adjustments (minutes with no rate are counted, never guessed) and is shown only to the principal and financial-authority holders; profit is billed less write-offs, invoiced expense cost and staff cost. Utilization stays on the report's capacity lines. Write-off and staff-cost records join ERASURE-002's billing and staff classes, retained rows, expiry redaction of reasons, invoice clocks and restore fence. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, BILL-003 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026).

**BILL-004 — Invoice reminders statements and bulk resend.** Overdue-invoice reminders run on a firm schedule (for example 3 days before the due date, on it, and 7, 14 and 30 days after) using MSG-001 templates. They stop when an invoice is paid, disputed or on a payment plan, and can be overridden per client. Staff can bulk resend selected invoices and generate monthly client statements of open invoices, credits and payments. Quick collect charges a saved method only within its PAY-001 authorization. Every reminder is recorded in the client's history. **Acceptance evidence:** Issue three invoices with different due dates, let the reminders run and pay one between steps; only the unpaid invoices are reminded, on schedule. Bulk resend two invoices. Generate a statement and reconcile it to open balances. Quick collect one invoice with an authorized saved card; a quick collect without authorization is refused. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** Invoice reminders send engagement class only, with MSG-002's send-time recheck. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, BILL-004 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026). **Implemented native slice (sx-blotter-c37, 22 Oct; reminder-consent default approved by ct 22 Oct 23:45Z):** reminders are automatic outbound mail, so the firm schedule runs only under a recorded consent of the principal or a financial-authority holder without client scopes: the steps in days from the due date (negative before it), one firm engagement-class MSG-001 template version and a reason, audited and step-up confirmed; pausing ends it. Each hourly run rechecks the consenter's live authority and the template version (otherwise the schedule pauses with a named reason), and for each issued invoice with an open balance, no dispute or payment-plan hold and a client not opted out, sends the latest passed step once (earlier passed steps are recorded as skipped, never sent late) to the invoice's billing contact with the numbered PDF, after MSG-002's engagement send-time recheck (active, authorized billing contact with email consent and no hard bounce); a refused recheck or placeholder holds that step, named, and is never replayed. A client follows the firm schedule, opts out or has its own steps; every reminder, hold and override is in the client's history. Paid means the invoice balance is zero after recorded receipts, deposits, credits or approved write-offs (BILL-003) and observed net settled provider payments. Bulk resend sends one reviewed preview of up to 50 issued invoices (their billing recipients, documents and one reason) through BILL-002's delivery. A client statement as of a date lists open issued invoices with aging, recorded credits and their applications, observed provider payment states and net amounts, and totals equal to the open balances; its CSV is an export. Quick collect requires PAY-001’s current invoice-bounded saved-method authorization and fresh-confirmed financial authority; its provider receipts update the same open balance. Any edit to reminder steps or the consented template version pauses the schedule and ends its consent. Reminder tables join the link and firm classes, erasure steps, expiry effects and observed provider/recipient copies; a restore returns the schedule paused and without consent, and claimed reminders held.

**BILL-005 — Payment gated delivery and credit hold.** A firm can require payment before releasing selected work product in the portal, such as a final return copy. The client sees the file as locked until paid. A card payment unlocks it on provider confirmation. For ACH the firm chooses whether a pending payment unlocks it or settlement is required. Records the client supplied are never withheld, consistent with Circular 230 §10.28; only the firm's own work product can be gated. Clients past a firm balance threshold go on credit hold: staff see the hold, and creating new work warns. A partner can override a gate or hold, with a recorded reason. **Acceptance evidence:** Gate a final return copy on an invoice. The client sees it locked, pays by card, and the file unlocks. With a wait-for-settlement ACH policy, the file stays locked until settlement. The client's own uploaded documents stay downloadable throughout. A partner override is recorded with its reason, and new work for an overdue client shows the credit hold. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Implemented semantics (ct approved with riders 22 Oct 23:45Z):** only a deliverable (the firm's own work product) can be gated, never a record the client supplied or any other file; the principal or a financial-authority holder gates a deliverable on one issued invoice of the same client, with a reason. Every version of a gated deliverable is withheld from the client portal, the portal file door and any bearer share link (HTTP 402 naming the invoice) until the invoice's gross is covered by applied credits, recorded deposits and observed net provider payments under the ACH policy; staff downloads are never gated. A write-off never releases a gate; only a partner (principal or financial-authority holder) override with a reason does, and it can be taken back. A receipt records how it was paid (card, ACH or other): a card or other receipt counts when recorded, an ACH deposit may be recorded pending until the bank settles it, and the firm policy (principal only, default: settlement required) chooses whether a pending ACH deposit releases a gated file. The same principal-only policy sets the credit-hold threshold (default: off) and grace days (default: 0): a client is on credit hold when the open balance of its issued invoices past due, after the grace days, is at least the threshold. Staff with client access see the hold on the client (amounts only if they may read billing); the job start, roll-forward and bulk schedule doors warn without blocking; a partner overrides or restores the hold with a reason, and any payment or write-off lowering the balance below the threshold ends the hold. **ACCESS-002 — Client permissions and sensitive data policies.** Configure least-privilege client/team/document access and separate partner financial authority, reviewer approval, preparer work, read-only staff and external-client identities. First configuration scopes every current staff member; no grant means no client access, including prior sessions, named-task access, API pages and agent context. New staff remain scoped. Client grants intersect the existing preparer/reviewer job role; read-only is a separate restriction refusing writes. Sensitive workpapers are internal to the principal and individually named staff with both client and job authority; restricting revokes contact grants and all existing shares. Permission changes invalidate concurrent writes, and notification/report dispatch rechecks current grants. The grant rechecks its consenting principal’s live owner authority. No person is created automatically and the principal is never managed by provisioning. No mapped group means no staff access; conflicting role mappings choose preparer. Existing direct client grants remain separate. Every lifecycle change revokes managed sessions, credential versions and agent keys. Native principal deactivation stays denied until the principal explicitly reactivates the member. Required enterprise sign-in fails closed during outages and after disconnection; native owner recovery retains the existing second-factor policy. A verified provider MFA assertion satisfies sign-in only, never sensitive-administration step-up. **ACCESS-004 — Enforced staff multi factor authentication.** The owner can set a firm policy requiring a second factor for every staff sign-in, whatever the method. Accepted factors are a TOTP authenticator app, a passkey or security key, or, under federated sign-in (ACCESS-005, ACCESS-003), an identity-provider assertion that MFA was performed. When the provider does not assert MFA, Blotter requires its own factor. The policy covers web, mobile and person-created API sessions. Integration and agent keys are separately scoped credentials (API-002, AGENT-001) and cannot be used to bypass it. A staff member must enroll before seeing any client data. Recovery uses one-time recovery codes, or an owner reset that is audited and revokes all of that person's sessions. The owner's own factor is recovered with recovery codes or by a second owner. Session lifetime and idle timeout are configurable. An enrollment report gives evidence for the firm's WISP and the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 CFR 314.4(c)(5)); it records enrollment facts and never claims certification. Every session, whenever it began, must pass its own second-factor check before any practice data, and a person who has enrolled a factor is asked for it at every new session even while the policy is off. Until a second owner role exists, the principal recovers their own factor with a recovery code. Until ACCESS-005 or ACCESS-003 passes a provider's MFA assertion to Blotter, every federated session is treated as lacking one and is challenged for a Blotter factor. Today's sessions are browser sign-in sessions, whatever the method, and all pass the same check; MOBILE-001 apps and API-002 person-created sessions inherit it before they ship. Session lifetime (from sign-in) and idle timeout (since the session's last request) are whole minutes set by the principal; reaching either ends the session. Five incorrect codes within 15 minutes pause verification for 15 minutes. **Acceptance evidence:** Enable the firm MFA policy. A preparer without a factor must enroll before seeing any client. Sign in with TOTP and with a passkey. A sign-in with the correct first factor and no second factor is refused, and a session created before the policy must step up before further access. When the preparer loses their factor, the owner resets it; the preparer's sessions are revoked and the audit shows who reset it. A federated sign-in whose token lacks an MFA assertion is challenged for a Blotter factor. Export the enrollment report.

**ACCESS-005 — Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 staff sign in.** Staff sign in with their firm Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 (Entra ID) account through OpenID Connect, so the firm's existing password, MFA and conditional-access policies apply to Blotter. The owner restricts sign-in to verified firm domains or tenant IDs, and each account maps to an invited Blotter member. Unknown accounts are refused and never created automatically. Blotter revalidates each federated identity at least hourly and on every API token refresh. A suspended or deleted account loses its Blotter session and API access at the next revalidation, or immediately when the provider sends a revocation signal (Google RISC, Microsoft continuous access evaluation). Native sign-in stays available for owner recovery, and the owner can disable it for staff. Signing in never grants mailbox access; that is a separate MAIL-001 grant. **Acceptance evidence:** Sign in one preparer through Google Workspace and another through Microsoft 365. A personal gmail.com account and an account from another tenant are refused. Suspend the Google account in Google Admin and confirm the Blotter browser session and that member's API token are refused within the revalidation interval, or immediately when the provider signal arrives. Disable the Microsoft user and confirm the same. The owner can still recover through native sign-in. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships.

**ACCESS-006 — Staff offboarding and ownership transfer.** Before deactivating a departing or long-absent staff member, the owner previews everything that person owns. That covers client ownership and team roles, open work and tasks, job roles, triaged email and their connected mailbox, scheduled reminders and automations, pending signature and document requests sent in their name, running timers and unapproved time. The owner transfers it to named successors in one reviewed batch. Messages already sent keep their original author. Future scheduled sends change sender only on approval. Deactivation revokes the person's sessions, API tokens and mailbox grants, and history keeps their attribution. **Acceptance evidence:** Give a preparer clients, open work, a scheduled reminder sequence, a pending signature request and a connected mailbox. Preview the transfer, reassign everything to two successors and deactivate the preparer. No orphaned item remains. The next reminder goes from the successor, past messages show the original author, and the deactivated member's sessions and tokens are refused. **Semantics (ACCESS-006):** the principal offboards (until a second owner role exists). The preview lists, for one member, active or already deactivated: open jobs where they are preparer, reviewer or manager (a client's ownership is its jobs and recurring rules until CRM-001 adds a client owner, which inherits this transfer before it ships); their open named tasks; recurring rules naming them; open tax notices assigned to them; open discussions they own; open client questions and client to-dos they own (PORTAL-003); agent proposals waiting for their decision; templates naming them as a task owner; their running timer; their time not yet approved; their live agent keys and sessions. The principal names a work successor (preparation, tasks, notices, discussions, client questions and to-dos, template tasks) and a review successor (review and manager roles, proposals; the work successor unless named). One batch, matching the preview exactly and refused while any job or rule would make someone review their own work, moves all of it, discards the running timer (nothing recorded; its start is kept in the audit), submits their unsubmitted time for approval on their behalf (returned entries never bill; the principal deletes them before closing their period), and deactivates them. Document requests move with their jobs; sent messages, reminders, decisions and recorded time keep their authors. AUTOMATE-001 versions remain principal-owned: the preview lists versions referencing the departing person and the batch checks those unchanged versions. It never silently transfers standing approval; live checks refuse an inactive assignee until a new version is reviewed. Deactivation, whether by offboarding or directly, revokes every session and agent key at once; reactivation needs a new sign-in and new keys, and a member deactivated urgently is offboarded the same way afterwards. Connected mailboxes, mail triage and mailbox grants (MAIL-001, MAIL-003), scheduled reminder sends (FOLLOWUP-001), signature requests (SIGN-001, SIGN-002) do not exist yet; each joins this preview and batch before it ships, and a scheduled send changes sender only through this approved batch. **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** A departing member's bulk-message batches move to the successor, and marketing batches need fresh principal approval. Implemented and asserted on MSG-002's doors (consent carriers journey, `tests/blotter/bulk-messages.test.mjs`); MSG-002 states the exact semantics.

**SECURE-001 — Security program and attestation.** Blotter publishes a security overview. Under NDA it provides firm owners with a current SOC 2 Type II report and bridge letter, a penetration-test summary, its subprocessor list, a data-flow description and a completed standard questionnaire (SIG Lite or CAIQ). It documents the controls a firm's WISP and the FTC Safeguards Rule rely on: encryption in transit and at rest, US data residency, access logging, tested backups and restores, vulnerability management, and incident response with customer notification within 72 hours of a confirmed incident affecting the firm's data. It also provides a WISP template that maps Blotter's controls to IRS Publications 4557 and 5708. Owners can export access logs. **Acceptance evidence:** As the owner, request and download the attestation package from settings, and check that the report period is current and the subprocessor list matches the enabled integrations. Export an access log for a date range. A preparer cannot download the package. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping.

**VAULT-001 — Client credential vault.** Clients and staff store client-provided logins, such as bank, payroll, state tax and sales-tax portal credentials, encrypted under per-firm keys. Each credential is visible only to staff permitted on that client. Every reveal requires the staff member's MFA step-up (ACCESS-004) and is logged. Clients add and update credentials through the portal. Credentials never appear in AI context, emails, search or plain exports; archives either encrypt or exclude them, at the owner's choice. Rotation reminders are optional. **Current semantics:** credentials are AES-GCM ciphertext under the firm's vault key, derived from the installation's own VAULT_KEY secret (never the session secret) and the firm's random salt; one installation is one firm, and without VAULT_KEY the vault refuses to store or reveal. Staff permitted on a client are the principal, reviewers and a preparer holding a job on that client (ACCESS-001 job scope; ACCESS-002 inherits configurable client grants before it ships); others get not found, and lists show names, portal addresses, authors, times and rotation dates only; usernames, passwords and notes stay sealed. A reveal needs a step-up from that session in the last 5 minutes: a fresh TOTP, passkey or recovery-code answer, even when the session already passed its sign-in check; agent keys never reveal. Every reveal and every refused reveal by permitted staff is logged with person, credential, time and outcome, and shows in the client's history. Clients add and replace credentials through their contact-scoped link (CRM-001 authority) and never read one back. Rotation dates show as due on the staff list; no reminder is sent. Archives carry the ciphertext (default), readable only where the same VAULT_KEY is configured, or leave it out; either way a restored credential that cannot be opened says so. The principal erases a credential by typing its name with a reason: the ciphertext goes, its name, authors, times and log stay, and older archives are fenced. A merged client's credentials follow its survivor. ERASURE-002 inherits client-wide credential erasure and holds, and MOBILE-001 inherits the native reveal, before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** A client adds a state sales-tax portal login through the portal. An assigned preparer reveals it after step-up, and the reveal is logged. An unassigned preparer cannot reveal it. The credential is absent from search, AI summaries and plain exports. Revoke the preparer's access and confirm their next reveal is refused. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Its owner erasure is refused inside an ERASURE-002 hold; whole-client erasure removes ciphertext, usernames and notes and keeps the reveal log under opaque labels (ERASURE-002).

**AGENT-001 — Agents prepare people approve.** A separately keyed agent reads role-scoped context and prepares roll-forward, reminder or billing-export proposals for its named human. Only that human may approve or decline. Accepted effects and decisions retain attribution/result identity; repeated decisions are refused and revoked keys cease working. Agent narrative never approves work or a bill. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a key, prepare all three proposal kinds, attempt approval with the key, approve as its human and decline another with a reason. Inspect decision/result history, refusal of a second decision and immediate key revocation.

Supporting private content stays at its current authorized source, with references in learning; versions and references are portable and source erasure retains the archive fence. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping.

**REVENUE-001 — Close billing leakage and reconciliation exceptions.** An agent compares accepted scope/amendments, time/budgets/WIP, retainer schedules, invoices, credits and provider/accounting events to detect missed charges, duplicate invoices and unreconciled collections. Draft evidence-backed fee amendments or corrections, then verify approved collections reconcile under the single invoice authority. Partners approve fees, amendments, messages, charges outside an existing mandate and write-offs; no narrative can turn pending ACH into settlement. **Acceptance evidence:** Introduce unbilled out-of-scope work, a duplicate invoice and an ACH return. Inspect cited exceptions and an amendment draft, approve one correction and decline another; reconcile confirmed provider events and leave the returned payment owned/open without duplicate charging or a silent write-off. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping.

**Native REVENUE-001 implementation:** The principal invokes a deterministic revenue assistant using an explicitly selected, reviewed ONBOARD-001 mapping of readable principal-recorded or SIGN-002 signed scope. Exact quotes and source integrity remain visible; a missing mapped work template is a review finding, never an independent legal interpretation. Approved, unreserved time and fees, recorded budgets, retainer definitions and amendments, invoice snapshots, credits and authenticated Stripe observations remain the source authorities. Suspected duplicates match work item, normalized title, currency and gross amount; the principal confirms whether they represent the same work. Approval can void only the cited current draft, atomically retaining the decision and billing-source reservations to prevent rebilling. An amendment approval records the reviewed draft only: the signed agreement, fee entitlements, delivery, collection and write-offs retain their separate explicit approvals. Evidence changes refuse stale approval. Returned and uncertain collections retain the invoice owner, due condition and no-automatic-retry next action; provider reconciliation reads current authenticated payment state, never charges or treats pending ACH as settlement. No external model, agent-key exposure, scheduled debit or new invoice authority is activated. Derived drafts obey native holds, erasure and inactive restoration; decisions and evidence are portable. Retainer comparisons use the first scheduled month, recorded work months and accepted amendment effective months; each period compares its accepted gross fee with non-void generated invoices. Future planned differences remain review findings. Principal-recorded firm-accounting event observations compare gross, net receipts, applied credits and approved write-offs with the selected native invoice authority; a later immutable event reference supersedes the earlier comparison for that source and invoice. These observations are source-reported evidence, never authenticated ledger-provider receipts, and cannot post to a ledger or change any financial authority. Accounting observations retain billing-class amounts and attribution with their invoice; native holds, reference redaction, archives and stale-restore fencing apply.

**ONBOARD-001 — Run new client onboarding to readiness.** An onboarding agent reads a signed engagement (ENGAGE-001, CRM-005) and proposes the complete setup. The plan covers clients and contacts per the scope, a work schedule from templates, requests for prior-year returns and opening balances, QBO and Xero and bank connection invitations, a 2848 or 8821 (AUTHZ-001) and portal invitations. Every item is linked to the scope it came from. Once a partner approves the plan, the agent sends only the approved invitations and requests, tracks responses and drafts targeted chases for missing setup items, and escalates a specific blocker to its owner. It cannot sign for anyone, connect accounts on a client's behalf, change fees or start billing. **Acceptance evidence:** Sign a new 1120-S and monthly bookkeeping engagement and inspect the proposed onboarding plan with its scope links. Approve it with one item removed. The agent sends only the approved invitations, tracks responses, and escalates a missing QBO connection to its owner. Nothing outside the approved plan is sent, and no fee or signature changes. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability and erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping. **Current native subset:** A principal explicitly maps exact readable quotes from a completed SIGN-002 document or an honestly labelled practitioner-recorded letter to tax and bookkeeping templates. Deterministic setup previews link every item to that source and its digest; they do not infer scope completeness. Review records selected and removed items once per signed source, with current source, contact and template checks. Observations retain earlier observations immutably and name the principal, evidence or blocker, next action and due condition; a received observation is never provider verification. This subset has no agent or model door and no execution or send authority. Restored reviews are held, and derived reviews join ERASURE-002 with its holds; removed or erased sources are refused. ct approved this principal-only review and observation subset on 25 October 2026 at 17:55Z: owner custody, audited review of signed scope, attributed immutable practitioner observations, no outbound execution and inactive held restoration. The complete partner and agent workflow remains an unbuilt obligation.

**SWITCH-001 — Plan and reconcile the switch from an incumbent.** A migration agent reads an authorized Karbon, TaxDome, Canopy, Financial Cents or Double export or API extract. It proposes the full mapping: work types and statuses (WORK-007), templates, custom fields, and source automations rewritten as paused AUTOMATE-001 rules. It explains every unmapped or lossy field with examples, proposes duplicate merges (CRM-004) and produces the reconciliation report. The owner corrects and approves the mapping. The agent never activates an automation, sends a message or charges a payment method, and its mapping runs only through the MIGRATE-001–005 import path. **Acceptance evidence:** Give the agent a Karbon export with custom statuses and automators. Inspect the proposed mapping, its examples and its unmapped-field explanations. Correct one status mapping and approve. Compare the reconciliation counts with the source, and confirm every rewritten automation is paused and no message was sent. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping.

**NOTICE-001 — Read notices and propose the response plan.** A notice agent reads an uploaded IRS or state notice, such as a CP2000, CP14, CP504, LT11 or a state equivalent. It extracts the notice type, tax year, amount and response deadline from the notice date. It checks for a recorded authorization (AUTHZ-001) and the latest transcripts (RESOLVE-001), and compares the notice items with the wage-and-income transcript. It then proposes the DUE-002 work item, the deadline, client questions and a response outline, each citing the notice lines. The practitioner approves the deadline, the work and any client message. The agent never contacts an agency or submits a response, and text inside the notice cannot instruct it. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload a CP2000 for a 1040 client. Compare the extracted fields with the notice text, and inspect the proposed deadline, the income items that differ from the wage-and-income transcript, and the draft client questions. Approve some questions and decline others. Overriding the deadline requires the practitioner. A misleading instruction embedded in the notice triggers no action. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability and erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping. **Approved native boundary (ct 25 Oct 20:20Z):** The same owner enablement, attestation, masking, audit, saved-draft and explicit-click rules as AI-001 apply. Only the principal or a reviewer prepares or reads a notice draft. Every extraction carries an exact source quote and a proposed verification warning. A person accepts or rejects each question and plan step; acceptance never changes a deadline, sends, posts, files or contacts an agency. The practitioner uses the separate native notice and message doors to adopt verified values or send their selected question. Recorded native taxpayer authorizations appear locally for review and are excluded from model input. IRS transcript context and comparison remain unavailable until RESOLVE-001 and INTEGRATE-006 are authorized; the response plan is a proposal, never legal or tax advice. **Implemented native processing:** The principal records the provider attestation reference, request budget and document review threshold. Each selected-source request reserves that budget before a single call through the existing provider module. Only saved output persists; current staff and source access are checked again after processing and on every saved-draft decision. Archives carry attributed history with enablement disabled; derived AI drafts obey retention holds, preview, erasure and stale restore fencing. Provider processing is listed as an observed outside copy under the recorded agreement, never as verified provider deletion.

A verified provider MFA assertion satisfies sign-in only, never sensitive-administration step-up. Archives restore connections and identities inactive, omit provisioning credentials and session assurance, and retain reviewed mappings; explicit audited erasure removes associations and fences older restores.

fragments.text: Native semantics: The principal invokes a deterministic revenue assistant using an explicitly selected, reviewed ONBOARD-001 mapping of readable principal-recorded or SIGN-002 signed scope. Exact quotes and source integrity remain visible; a missing mapped work template is a review finding, never an independent legal interpretation. Approved, unreserved time and fees, recorded budgets, retainer definitions and amendments, invoice snapshots, credits and authenticated Stripe observations remain the source authorities. Suspected duplicates match work item, normalized title, currency and gross amount; the principal confirms whether they represent the same work. Approval can void only the cited current draft, atomically retaining the decision and billing-source reservations to prevent rebilling. An amendment approval records the reviewed draft only: the signed agreement, fee entitlements, delivery, collection and write-offs retain their separate explicit approvals. Evidence changes refuse stale approval. Returned and uncertain collections retain the invoice owner, due condition and no-automatic-retry next action; provider reconciliation reads current authenticated payment state, never charges or treats pending ACH as settlement. No external model, agent-key exposure, scheduled debit or new invoice authority is activated. Derived drafts obey native holds, erasure and inactive restoration; decisions and evidence are portable. Retainer comparisons use the first scheduled month, recorded work months and accepted amendment effective months; each period compares its accepted gross fee with non-void generated invoices. Future planned differences remain review findings. Principal-recorded firm-accounting event observations compare gross, net receipts, applied credits and approved write-offs with the selected native invoice authority; a later immutable event reference supersedes the earlier comparison for that source and invoice. These observations are source-reported evidence, never authenticated ledger-provider receipts, and cannot post to a ledger or change any financial authority. Accounting observations retain billing-class amounts and attribution with their invoice; native holds, reference redaction, archives and stale-restore fencing apply.

Additional evidence: Taxable retainer gross before generation, removal after generation and restoration after voiding; a settled collection with independently asserted recorded and native receipts of 10,000 cents and no differences; attributed once-only preparation and accounting audit events, including actor, action, client, exact detail and bounded time, with replay adding none, are asserted by `tests/blotter/revenue-proof.mjs` / assertRevenueFlow and assertRevenueAudit and `tests/blotter/revenue-custody.mjs` / assertRevenueCustody and assertRevenueErasure. The same journey preserves closed approved source time, refuses correction of an issued duplicate, matches nonzero applied credits and write-offs, and refuses both accounting doors after principal revocation. Archived clients refuse both new accounting observations and exact replay; amendment decisions preserve invoice authority and provider charge counts.
